articles.title: Super Bowl LXI lands on Valentine’s Day for the first time in history creating an unusual football-versus-romance showdown
articles.summary: NFL News: Super Bowl LXI is about to create a very unusual sporting dilemma. The NFL’s championship game is scheduled for February 14, 2027, putting it on Valen.
articles.body: Super Bowl LXI is about to create a very unusual sporting dilemma. The NFL’s championship game is scheduled for February 14, 2027, putting it on Valentine’s Day for the first time in Super Bowl history. With romance and football competing for the same Sunday, fans have already begun joking about dinner reservations, watch parties and the ultimate relationship compromise.Super Bowl LXI and Valentine’s Day create a unique clashThe date alone is enough to make the 2027 Super Bowl stand out. The game will take place at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, on February 14, meaning couples will have to decide how they want to spend one of the biggest nights on the American sporting calendar.For football fans, the answer may seem obvious. For couples with different priorities, however, the evening could require some negotiation.Social media has already embraced the idea. One Reddit commenter joked about the pressure on restaurants, writing:"The Valentine's Day brunch reservations are going to be harder to get than a Super Bowl ticket."Another post took the joke even further, imagining the holiday as a test of romantic loyalty:"Super Bowl on Valentine's? Peak relationship apocalypse incoming—guys choosing touchdowns over touchy-feely dates. Ladies, demand a halftime proposal or it's single season next year."The humor works because the conflict is so easy to imagine. A romantic dinner could overlap with pregame coverage. A reservation might clash with kickoff. And anyone hosting a Super Bowl party could suddenly find themselves planning around Valentine's Day expectations.There is also a convenient escape route. The game falls on Presidents' Day weekend, giving many people the chance to turn the occasion into a longer celebration. Couples could celebrate Valentine's Day on Saturday, watch the Super Bowl on Sunday and use Monday to recover from the late night.Super Bowl 2027 brings another major change for NFL fansThe unusual date is not the only reason Super Bowl LXI will be significant. ESPN will broadcast the championship game for the first time in network history, with ABC also carrying the event. ESPN has already outlined extensive programming and storytelling designed to build anticipation well before the game itself.The timing also feeds into a broader conversation about the Super Bowl calendar. The NFL has long faced calls to make the Monday after the championship game a national holiday, particularly because fans already tend to treat Presidents' Day weekend as a natural extension of Super Bowl celebrations.Commissioner Roger Goodell has previously discussed how changes to the NFL schedule could eventually push the Super Bowl toward Presidents' Day weekend. In comments cited in the original report, he said:"I think if you went to 18 weeks regular season that would probably occur," Goodell said at the time. "It is possible somewhere in the calendar. Could happen before that just because of the calendar, the way it lays out. But I think 18 weeks would get you to that point, and I think it would be a really great move."For now, February 14, 2027 remains a one-of-a-kind collision between football and romance. The NFL has confirmed the date, and fans have plenty of time to decide whether Super Bowl Sunday will be a date-night disaster, a couples' tradition or simply the perfect excuse to order wings and watch football together.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Inspiring story of the day: “She’s my everything. I love her” How Tom Brady’s mother Galynn defied cancer and stood by the star QB through adversity and his historic Super Bowl comeback
articles.summary: NFL News: Success stories are often remembered through championships and records, but Tom Brady’s 2016 season also came with a difficult time for his family. Wh.
articles.body: Success stories are often remembered through championships and records, but Tom Brady’s 2016 season also came with a difficult time for his family. While Brady served a four-game suspension, his mother, Galynn, was undergoing treatment for stage 2 breast cancer, including chemotherapy and radiation.Unable to attend his regular-season games, Galynn watched from home before making it to Super Bowl LI, where she watched Brady lead the Patriots back from 28-3 to beat Atlanta 34-28. After the victory, Brady said, “She’s my everything. I just love her so much.”How Galynn Brady’s cancer diagnosis changed the family’s 2016 seasonTom Brady's mother, Galynn's cancer battle began in the summer of 2016. In an interview with NFL correspondent Andrea Kremer, she remembered sitting in a doctor's office when she was told that she had breast cancer. Doctors told her it was stage 2, but she also learned that the cancer was fast-growing and aggressive.“I just remember sitting in the doctor’s office and them telling me ‘You have breast cancer. It’s only stage 2,’” Galynn recalled. “And so the journey began.”That journey involved five months of chemotherapy, followed by radiation and other treatment. The diagnosis immediately changed the family's routine because Galynn had traditionally been a regular presence at Tom's games. During the 2016 season, however, her health prevented her from travelling to Patriots games.Instead, football became something she watched from home while concentrating on treatment. Her husband, Tom Brady Sr., later explained how the family structured its weeks around Galynn's chemotherapy and Tom's games.“Everything centered around 10 o'clock Thursday morning” for her chemotherapy and then Sunday morning when the family would watch football, he explained. Even while dealing with cancer, Galynn continued following her son's season. Those Sunday games gave the family a familiar routine during months that were anything but normal.How Tom Brady supported his mother while facing his own adversityGalynn's illness was not the only major challenge facing the Brady family that season. Tom entered 2016 dealing with the fallout from the Deflategate controversy and a four-game suspension.For Brady, watching his mother go through cancer treatment while also dealing with his own public struggles was emotionally difficult. Years later, while discussing that period in Man in the Arena, he explained how painful it had been for Galynn to see her son publicly criticised.“I think, personally, that was very difficult for her to see her son kind of raked through the coals like I was,” Brady said.He believed his mother had already been carrying the stress of her own illness, so seeing what was happening to her son added another burden. The family therefore became an important source of support for both Galynn and Tom.During his suspension, Brady spent time with his family at Pebble Beach in California. His ex wife Gisele Bündchen, daughter Vivian, nieces and nephews were also there. Brady later recalled standing on the 18th hole and looking around at the people closest to him while thinking about what really mattered.“Being with my family at a very vulnerable time,” he said, gave him a different perspective.Instead of allowing football to consume every part of his life, Brady recognised that his mother's health and his family's well-being deserved his attention too.How Galynn Brady fought through treatment with one goal in mindAs the Patriots' season continued and the team moved closer to another Super Bowl appearance, the Brady family began thinking about whether Galynn would be healthy enough to attend.Tom Brady told his parents that she would be ready for the Super Bowl. According to Tom Brady Sr., the family had calculated that the end of Galynn's five months of chemotherapy would fall about two weeks before the championship game.Galynn completed her final round of chemotherapy on January 12, 2017. But her recovery did not immediately become easy. She developed pneumonia and shingles, leaving her ability to travel to Houston in doubt.Her doctor did not clear her for the trip until one day before the family was scheduled to leave.Galynn could have stayed home after everything she had endured, but she wanted to see her son play.“There’s a special bond between a mother and a son,” Galynn said. “I just wanted to be there for Tommy, and I wanted to be there with our family. Everybody was going to the Super Bowl and I didn’t want to miss that.”Those words explain why reaching Houston meant so much to her. She had spent months watching Tom from home while going through chemotherapy, but she wanted to be beside him and her family when the Patriots reached the biggest game of the season.Her determination also showed how she approached the cancer battle itself. She was not allowing the illness to completely take away the moments she valued most.How Super Bowl LI became Galynn Brady victory tooGalynn finally made it to Houston, but the game itself quickly became another test for the family.The Patriots fell behind the Atlanta Falcons 28-3, leaving New England with a massive deficit to overcome. Galynn watched from the stands as the team struggled, and the situation became so painful that she eventually told her husband she wanted to leave.“I said to Tom, ‘I just want to go home,’” she later recalled. “I was heartbroken for Tommy.”Tom, however, continued fighting. The Patriots gradually erased the deficit and eventually forced overtime. New England completed the comeback with a 34-28 victory, giving Brady his fifth Super Bowl championship and the Patriots the largest comeback in Super Bowl history.For Galynn, the emotion was overwhelming after everything she had experienced.“I’m so glad that I decided I would go and just put cancer aside for that weekend,” she later said. She had made it to Houston despite the complications that had threatened her recovery, and she was there to watch her son produce one of the most remarkable comebacks in NFL history.Why Robert Kraft gave Galynn Brady her own Super Bowl ringThe Patriots' victory gave the Brady family a moment they would never forget, but Robert Kraft added another deeply personal gesture afterward. The Patriots owner gave Galynn her own Super Bowl ring, recognising her connection to the team's unforgettable championship season. Kraft's gesture acknowledged what she had endured while Tom was leading New England toward the title.For Galynn, the ring represented much more than the Patriots' victory. It was connected to the months of chemotherapy, the health complications, the uncertainty over whether she could travel and the decision to put her illness aside long enough to be there for her son.How Galynn Brady recovery brought another reason for Tom Brady’s family to celebrateThe Super Bowl did not mark the end of Galynn's recovery, but it was an important milestone. In June 2017, Tom Brady Sr. said that Galynn had finished her cancer treatment about two months earlier and was doing well, playing golf and tennis again.In August, Tom Brady gave another encouraging update, saying his mother was “on the road to recovery” after receiving very positive test results. “She’s doing really well,” Brady said. “Everyone in our family is so happy.”By October, reports said Galynn's latest cancer screening had come back clear, although her cancer carried a high risk of recurrence. She continued to undergo regular testing as part of her follow-up care.Her experience also encouraged her to share a message with other people facing cancer. Galynn said she hoped people could learn from her story and keep a positive attitude rather than giving up hope.“I would hope that they would learn to keep a positive attitude, and not to give up hope,” she said. “Be thankful every day; think about the people that are caring about you.”That is perhaps the most directly inspirational message from Galynn herself, because it came from someone who had actually gone through the treatment she was describing.How Galynn’s strength became part of Tom Brady’s storyGalynn had supported Tom long before he became one of the most successful quarterbacks in NFL history. She was there throughout his career and remained one of the people closest to him, but her cancer battle showed just how strong their bond had become.In 2016, both mother and son were facing challenges that demanded patience and resilience. Tom had to deal with suspension and the pressure surrounding his career, while Galynn had to endure chemotherapy, radiation and serious health complications.Neither could simply remove the other's struggle, but they continued encouraging each other.Tom's support was important to Galynn during treatment, especially when she struggled with the physical changes brought by chemotherapy. She later recalled losing her hair and wearing a bandanna, while Tom would reassure her by telling her she looked beautiful.Galynn, meanwhile, gave Tom another reason to keep pushing when the Patriots faced their biggest challenge of the season.Her decision to travel to Houston brought their two journeys together. She had fought through cancer treatment to be there, and Tom responded with one of the greatest performances of his career.That is what makes Galynn Brady's story so powerful. She was not simply watching her son play football while recovering from cancer. She was actively fighting her own battle, trying to stay positive and refusing to let the illness take away the moments she wanted to share with her family. Tom Brady's Super Bowl LI comeback will always be remembered for the 28-3 deficit, the overtime victory and another championship for one of the NFL's greatest quarterbacks. For the Brady family, however, the night carried a much deeper meaning.Galynn had fought through cancer to sit in those stands. Tom had fought through his own adversity to lead the Patriots back. When the two finally embraced after the victory, the moment represented everything they had endured together.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: How did Travis Kelce go from a $531,000 salary in 2014 to a $90 million net worth and what comes after football?
articles.summary: Travis Kelce's 2026 salary with the Kansas City Chiefs is $12 million. Fully guaranteed.
articles.body: Travis Kelce's 2026 salary with the Kansas City Chiefs is $12 million. Fully guaranteed. That number alone would be a career highlight for most NFL players. But for Kelce, it barely scratches the surface of a financial story that includes $123 million in career NFL earnings, a $100 million podcast deal with Amazon's Wondery, and a real estate portfolio worth millions more. Twelve years after signing for $531,000 as a rookie, the tight end has quietly built one of the most diversified wealth portfolios in professional football.How did Travis Kelce build a $90 million net worth from the NFL?The math on Travis Kelce's NFL earnings is straightforward, even if the journey wasn't. He signed his first professional contract in 2013 for $3.12 million over four years. By 2014, he was collecting $531,000 for the season. Three years later, after proving himself as one of the most dangerous receiving tight ends in the league, Kansas City handed him a five-year, $46 million extension.That deal was followed by another in 2020, then a renegotiated two-year agreement in April 2024 worth $34.25 million, briefly making him the highest-paid tight end in football. Through the 2025 season, Kelce had pulled in approximately $111.2 million in NFL salary and bonuses alone. His current $12 million deal for 2026 will push that career total to roughly $123.2 million by season's end.The on-field numbers back every dollar. Seven straight 1,000-yard seasons between 2016 and 2022 remain an NFL record for tight ends. His 20 postseason receiving touchdowns are the most ever at his position. Three Super Bowl rings. The case for his contracts was never really a debate.What is Travis Kelce's $100 million podcast deal with Wondery?The podcast deal is where Kelce's earnings story gets genuinely interesting. In August 2024, Travis and his brother Jason signed a three-year, $100 million distribution agreement with Amazon's Wondery for their show, *New Heights with Jason and Travis Kelce*. The brothers had launched the weekly podcast in 2022, and it grew steadily on the back of football analysis and sibling chemistry before exploding into mainstream territory when Travis began dating Taylor Swift in 2023.The $100 million headline figure needs context, though. The revenue is split between both brothers, covers production costs, management fees, and taxes, and is spread across three years. Still, it represents something significant: Kelce generating serious income entirely independent of football, in a format with far more longevity than a tight end's playing career.What does Travis Kelce's financial future look like after football?Kelce's business portfolio reads less like an athlete's side project and more like a deliberate post-career plan. He holds equity in Casa Azul Tequila, Garage Beer, Hilo Nutrition, and Club Car Wash. He co-owns 1587 Prime, a Kansas City steakhouse built with Patrick Mahomes. He has endorsement deals with Nike, State Farm, McDonald's, T-Mobile, and several others. His two properties in Missouri and Kansas carry a combined value worth of $7 million.Then there is the media side. A hosting stint on Saturday Night Live. A role in Ryan Murphy's Grotesquerie. A game show hosting gig on 'Are You Smarter Than a Celebrity?' for Prime Video. The camera clearly works for him, and the entertainment industry has noticed.At 36, Kelce's NFL days are numbered. But the infrastructure he has built across podcasting, equity investments, real estate, and television positions him well beyond whatever his final NFL paycheck looks like. The $531,000 season in 2014 was the beginning of a long build. The $90 million net worth is not the ceiling.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Inspiring story on motherhood: "It's probably the hardest thing I've ever done in my life...it's the most daunting task" - How Donna Kelce navigated the challenges of raising Jason and Travis Kelce
articles.summary: NFL News: For Donna Kelce, motherhood was never simply about getting her children through childhood. It meant working hard, making difficult choices and giving .
articles.body: For Donna Kelce, motherhood was never simply about getting her children through childhood. It meant working hard, making difficult choices and giving Jason and Travis Kelce the freedom to discover who they were. Years before they became NFL stars, she was a working mother trying to keep family life steady. In 2024, she opened up about just how demanding that journey had been.Donna Kelce’s powerful words about motherhoodDonna Kelce shared her candid thoughts on motherhood during a Glamour group interview published on October 3, 2024. The conversation was part of Glamour’s 2024 Women of the Year feature, which brought together Donna, Tina Knowles, Maggie Baird and Mandy Teefey to discuss raising children who would eventually become major figures in sports, music and entertainment.Asked about what motherhood had been like for her, Donna did not describe it as an effortless or glamorous experience. Instead, she focused on the responsibility that comes with raising children who depend on you for almost everything.She said:“Being a mom is probably the hardest thing I’ve ever done in my life. It’s so much easier to just go to work.”..Donna Kelce then explained that raising children means trying to make the best choices possible while dealing with limited resources and the constant responsibility of caring for people who rely on you. She ultimately described motherhood as the most daunting task she had ever taken on.The honesty in her answer is striking because it came from someone whose sons would later become two of the most recognizable names in American football. Yet Donna was not talking about fame when she made the comment. She was talking about the everyday work of being a mother.That distinction matters.Raising Jason and Travis Kelce was never just about footballJason Kelce and Travis Kelce did not begin their childhoods with a clear path toward professional football. Donna told Glamour that the brothers tried several sports, including hockey, lacrosse and basketball. Football came later, when they reached seventh grade.Even then, Donna Kelce did not immediately know that her sons would build professional careers from the sport.She said the possibility became clearer only when college recruiting letters began arriving. Until that point, she was simply watching two athletic boys grow, compete and find interests of their own.That detail gives her motherhood comments more weight.The woman who eventually became known around the NFL as “Mama Kelce” was not raising two guaranteed stars. She was raising children without knowing where their talents would eventually take them. Her job was to give them room to grow while keeping them grounded.Donna Kelce has also spoken about the energetic nature of her sons as children. During the same Glamour conversation, she recalled broken windows and calls from neighbors, while making clear that Jason and Travis were not bad children. They were simply energetic and, as she put it, rambunctious.Those memories offer a very different picture from the polished image fans now see..Before the Super Bowl appearances, championship celebrations and packed stadiums, there were ordinary family moments. There were mistakes, sports practices, neighborhood adventures and the countless small responsibilities that come with raising children.Donna Kelce was also building a careerAnother important part of Donna’s story is that motherhood did not happen in isolation.She was also working.Donna had a career in banking and later described herself as a major breadwinner in her family. She told Glamour that she worked extremely hard because she wanted to move forward professionally. At the same time, she believed it was important for her children to see that a woman could build a career and pursue her own ambitions.That balance adds another layer to her comments about motherhood.For Donna, going to work could be demanding, but parenting carried a different kind of responsibility. A job has defined duties, deadlines and hours. Raising children is far less predictable. It follows you home. It changes as children grow. And there is no simple measure for whether you are doing it right.Her reflections also touched on her marriage to Ed Kelce. Donna said the couple knew their marriage was no longer working but chose to remain together for their children for a period of time. She described their relationship as friendly and said they wanted to keep life as normal as possible for Jason and Travis.Eventually, Donna said she had to move forward on her own.That part of her story shows that her definition of motherhood was not limited to the visible moments. It included personal sacrifices and decisions that her sons may not have fully understood while they were growing up.The values behind Jason and Travis Kelce’s successDonna Kelce’s influence becomes easier to understand when looking at how she talks about her sons today.She has consistently emphasized supporting children rather than forcing them into a particular future. In the Glamour interview, she explained that parents learn more about their children as they encounter people and experiences outside their immediate community. Her approach was to support what her children loved and encourage them to enjoy it.That philosophy appears to have shaped the Kelce family.Jason eventually became a Super Bowl champion with the Philadelphia Eagles and one of the most respected centers of his generation. Travis established himself as one of the NFL’s premier tight ends with the Kansas City Chiefs.Their achievements are enormous. But Donna's comments suggest that she measures success differently.For her, keeping her sons grounded mattered just as much as celebrating their accomplishments.She told Glamour that she would remind Jason and Travis of their childhood when fame became overwhelming. The goal was simple: remind them where they came from and help them remember that they were still the same people they had always been.That perspective became especially meaningful as both brothers entered a world where almost every part of their lives could attract public attention.Why Donna Kelce’s motherhood confession still resonatesDonna Kelce’s description of motherhood stands out because it cuts through the glamour surrounding her family.Today, Jason and Travis are household names. Their games attract millions of viewers, their personal lives generate constant headlines and their family has become part of the wider sports conversation.But Donna’s story began somewhere much quieter.It began with a mother working, raising two boys and trying to make good decisions without knowing exactly where those decisions would lead.Her statement to Glamour was powerful because she did not present motherhood as a perfect journey. She acknowledged the pressure, uncertainty and sacrifice involved. She also recognized that the work of raising children often happens without applause.That may be the most revealing part of her story.The world sees the Super Bowl rings, the records and the stadium lights. Donna remembers the years before all of that. She remembers the children who needed her, the choices she had to make and the effort required to help them become independent adults.Her famous sons may now be the stars, but Donna’s words offer a reminder that behind many extraordinary careers is a much more ordinary story: a parent showing up, day after day, and doing the best they can.And for Donna Kelce, that was the hardest job of all.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "I'm grateful for every lesson": Gisele Bündchen’s candid Tom Brady divorce admission revealed the pain behind her new beginning
articles.summary: NFL News: Gisele Bündchen’s divorce from Tom Brady is no longer breaking news, but a deeply emotional 2024 interview still offers a revealing look at what the s.
articles.body: Gisele Bündchen’s divorce from Tom Brady is no longer breaking news, but a deeply emotional 2024 interview still offers a revealing look at what the supermodel went through after their marriage ended. During a conversation with ABC News’ Robin Roberts, Bündchen struggled to hold back tears while reflecting on the end of a 13-year marriage, her children and the new chapter she was trying to build.Gisele Bündchen opens up about Tom Brady divorceThe interview, released in March 2024 as part of “IMPACT x Nightline: Gisele Bündchen: Climbing the Mountain,” came more than a year after Bündchen and Brady finalized their divorce in October 2022.Their split ended a relationship that had lasted 16 years and a marriage that had lasted 13. By the time Bündchen sat down with Roberts, however, she was trying to understand the experience as part of a larger personal transition rather than simply an ending.Roberts reminded her that she had previously described the divorce as “the death of a dream.” The comment immediately struck an emotional chord.“Well, when you say ...” the model began, before pausing and getting teary. “Sorry, guys, I didn't know ... can I have a little moment?”After collecting herself, Bündchen spoke about accepting a future she had never expected to have.“It's definitely a time of, you know, a transition that had to take place, and it's not something that you — I don't think you wish for that, you know?” she said. “But I think sometimes in life things happen. I feel so blessed because, like, I wouldn't change anything in my life. I had incredible experiences. I learned so much. I have my children, which are the biggest blessings in my life.“And now I get to create — it's a new season, a new chapter in my life, and I get to learn new things, and I get to walk my path in a different way, you know?“And I'm grateful for all of it. I'm grateful for every lesson.”Her words showed that the divorce was not something she viewed in simple terms. There was pain, but there was also gratitude for the years she shared with Brady and the family they created.Gisele Bündchen focuses on her children after divorceBündchen and Brady share two children, Benjamin and Vivian. Brady also has a son, Jack, with actress Bridget Moynahan. For Bündchen, co-parenting meant accepting that the children would grow up moving between two different households and sets of rules.“There's easier days than others. But it's amazing that the kids — they're super smart children,” Bündchen said, laughing. “They know what they can get away with. So I think it's natural that it has different rules, and kids just adapt and they're going to try to do what they want. And I can only control what I do.”She also emphasized the value of her children having relationships with both parents.“It's amazing that they get to spend time with both parents because it's more enriching for their lives, two different worlds, and they get to learn from two different worlds.”Bündchen spoke warmly about Brady’s oldest son, Jack, whom she helped raise during her years with the former NFL star.“I raised him. I love him,” she said.Looking ahead, Bündchen said she wanted to live according to her own values rather than public expectations.“I'm very committed to living my truth more than ever, so I would say that's where my heart is now, where I am right now. I'm living my truth and I'm not apologizing for it,” she explained.The 2024 interview remains significant because it captured Bündchen at a vulnerable point in her life. She was not simply discussing a famous divorce. She was describing the difficult process of accepting change, protecting her children and finding an identity beyond a marriage that had once shaped so much of her public life.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: “Seeing the smiles on these kids. I will remember..”: How Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce’s act of kindness brought smiles, gifts and a year of relief to a Kansas City family in need
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce gave a Kansas City family a surprise they never saw coming. On Nov. 14, 2018, the two Kansas City Chiefs stars walked.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce gave a Kansas City family a surprise they never saw coming. On Nov. 14, 2018, the two Kansas City Chiefs stars walked into the Guadalupe Center with food, holiday gifts and a special message for a mother raising four children.What started as a routine visit quickly became an emotional afternoon. Mahomes and Kelce spent time with the children, while the Guadalupe Centers and Kansas City Southern revealed that the family would receive help paying its home utilities for an entire year.Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce turned a holiday surprise into a year of reliefMaria arrived at the Guadalupe Center in downtown Kansas City with her four children, 12-year-old Eulises, 11-year-old Alfredo, 5-year-old Gael and 3-year-old Sofia. She expected a normal check-in, but Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce soon walked through the door carrying baskets filled with food and gifts. Mahomes immediately made the moment personal. He handed Sofia a doll, found a superhero toy for Gael, Legos for Alfredo and a football for Eulises. The children quickly settled into their gifts, but the biggest surprise had not arrived yet.Representatives from Kansas City Southern and the Guadalupe Centers then told Maria that they would cover her family's home utility costs for a full calendar year through the Guadalupe Centers' Family Support Services program. Maria had a chronic condition that made it difficult to make ends meet, so the assistance offered more than a memorable holiday moment. It removed one major household expense for a mother caring for four children.Maria, speaking through a translator during the Nov. 14 visit, captured the shock of the moment by saying, “It was a grand surprise. The first thing I thought was just, ‘Wow.’” She then explained what the support meant for her family: “This is going to be such a huge help. My family will always remember this.”The money came through the Hunt Family Foundation 50/50 raffle from the Chiefs' Week 7 matchup against the Cincinnati Bengals on Oct. 21, 2018. Kansas City Southern had nominated the Guadalupe Centers as the beneficiary, and the raffle raised $56,925 for the organization. The donation later grew into a $60,000 contribution that supported the Guadalupe Centers' family support work.But Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce did not simply hand over gifts and leave. They stayed for nearly an hour and spent time with each child. Mahomes showed Eulises how to grip his new football, while Kelce talked with Alfredo about school. That interaction caught the attention of Diane Rojas, then vice president of Health and Social Services at Guadalupe Centers, who said the players' engagement with the children stood out because they knew who the Chiefs were and appreciated the unusual excitement of meeting them.Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce showed why the gesture meant more than the giftsThe personal connection made the afternoon even more meaningful. During the Nov. 14, 2018 visit at the Guadalupe Center, Mahomes explained why he took the moment seriously. “It meant a ton to be part of that, and not just for me, but for the family,” the Chiefs quarterback said. He also praised Maria, adding, “That mom does so much and those kids are great kids. She earned everything that she got today and a thousand times more.”Kelce saw the same bond when he spent time with the children. Speaking after the Guadalupe Center visit, he said, “This was a special group right here – they were picked by the Guadalupe Center for a reason.” He also pointed to the relationship between Maria and her children, saying, “You could tell how much this mother loves her four kids and on top of that, you can see how much those kids love their mother. It was all-around just a fun experience to be here.”In Maria’s case, however, the meaning went beyond one afternoon. “This means everything to me. My kids will always remember what happened here today,” she said during the event. “They’ll never forget this.”Travis Kelce felt the same way. After seeing the children enjoy the day, he offered the line that captured the entire moment: “Seeing the smiles on these kids’ faces [was special]. I’ll remember this day forever.”The visit also came during a wider week of community work. On Nov. 12, 2018, the Chiefs Community Caring Team visited Guadalupe Center Middle School for a Play 60 clinic involving more than two dozen children. Two days later, Mahomes and Kelce brought a different kind of support directly to a family in need.For the Kansas City Chiefs stars, it was a community appearance. For Maria and her children, it meant gifts, personal attention and a full year without the burden of their home utility bills. That is why Kelce's words still fit the moment: it was a day worth remembering.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: South Middle School football game halted after 16-year-old girl ‘attacks’ player, faces assault and disorderly conduct charges
articles.summary: NFL News: A 16-year-old girl is facing assault and disorderly conduct charges after she ran onto the field during a middle school football game in Winchester, T.
articles.body: A 16-year-old girl is facing assault and disorderly conduct charges after she ran onto the field during a middle school football game in Winchester, Tennessee, and tackled a South Middle School player. The incident happened Tuesday night during the game against Cornersville Middle School at Franklin County High School. Game officials stopped the game and the stadium was cleared. No injuries were reported, according to WSMV and the Franklin County Sheriff’s Office.16-year-old girl tackles South Middle School football playerThe incident began after South Middle School scored a touchdown and an extra point. According to WSMV, a scuffle then started between two players from the teams. Investigators said the 16-year-old girl, who is from Marshall County, ran onto the field and went straight toward the South Middle School player involved in that exchange.Video from the game shows the girl coming from the stands and making contact with the player, sending both to the ground. The player got back up, but the girl pushed him down again. A person who appeared to be a coach then stepped in and stopped the confrontation.The girl left the field afterward, but a school resource officer met her as she was leaving. She was later released to her parents, who were at the game. The Franklin County Sheriff’s Office said she was charged with assault and disorderly conduct.The reason she ran onto the field has not been confirmed by authorities. Reports only connect her actions to the scuffle that followed South Middle School’s touchdown. There is no official information showing what, if anything, happened between the girl and the player before she entered the field.South Middle School football game ends early after field incidentReferees ended the game after the girl entered the field. Officials cleared the playing area and then emptied the stadium. The game between South Middle School and Cornersville Middle School did not continue.NewsChannel 5 reported that no one was injured in the incident. The Franklin County Sheriff’s Office also confirmed that the girl was released to her parents after she was taken into custody.The school consequences are also serious. Franklin County Schools issued a lifetime ban keeping the girl off all district properties. The Tennessee Secondary School Athletic Association separately banned her from attending Cornersville Middle School home and away athletic events for one year.The game was played at Franklin County High School because South uses that venue for home games. The Tennessee Secondary School Athletic Association confirmed the one-year event ban. The incident was captured on video and circulated in reports about the game.WSMV reported that South Middle School’s principal praised the staff, coaches and school resource officers for how they handled the situation.The girl’s identity has not been made public because she is 16. The available reports do not say whether she has a lawyer or give further details about the juvenile case. Authorities have not publicly stated what led to the confrontation beyond the scuffle involving the players.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: How far will Jerry Jones go to punish Donovan Ezeiruaku? Cowboys’ $500K fine after Saints Brawl raises questions
articles.summary: NFL News: Jerry Jones is not letting Donovan Ezeiruaku walk away from the Cowboys-Saints brawl without consequences. The Dallas Cowboys owner plans to appeal th.
articles.body: Jerry Jones is not letting Donovan Ezeiruaku walk away from the Cowboys-Saints brawl without consequences. The Dallas Cowboys owner plans to appeal the team’s $500,000 NFL fine, but he has also confirmed that players involved in the fights will receive fines from Dallas.Ezeiruaku stands out because Jones indicated he will be among those players fined. The second-year linebacker was ejected after throwing a punch at Saints center Erik McCoy, making this more than just another heated training-camp moment.Jerry Jones confirms Donovan Ezeiruaku will face the Dallas Cowboys fineDallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones has answered the biggest question surrounding Donovan Ezeiruaku. The Cowboys owner indicated that the young linebacker will receive a team fine after his role in the fight with New Orleans Saints center Erik McCoy.Jones spoke about the situation after the NFL fined the Cowboys and Saints $500,000 each for the repeated altercations during their joint practice. He made it clear that Dallas will handle the players separately from the league’s punishment.“I think that you have to have consequences, and that needs to register,” Jones said while speaking to reporters in Oxnard after the Cowboys completed their final training-camp practice there. He added that players need to understand the consequences of their behavior.That directly answers how far Jones plans to go with Ezeiruaku. The Cowboys will not simply accept the NFL fine and move forward. The team will also take money from the players responsible for the incidents.Jones has not announced the exact amount Ezeiruaku will pay. However, he indicated that Ezeiruaku is one of the Cowboys players who will receive a fine.The punishment comes after a chaotic joint practice that featured several fights between Dallas and New Orleans. Players from both sides exchanged punches, joined confrontations away from their original practice fields and pushed the session close to cancellation.The Cowboys and Saints coaches had to discuss whether they should end the practice early. Schottenheimer later said the session became too “chippy” and admitted that the teams did not get enough of the work they wanted.Ezeiruaku became one of the most visible Cowboys players in the chaos. He got into it with McCoy and threw a punch, leading officials to eject him.The bigger concern for Dallas is that this was his second ejection for throwing a punch during training camp. That makes the internal fine more than a simple response to one bad moment. The Cowboys now need Ezeiruaku to show that he can control his emotions while keeping the physical edge they want from him.Why Donovan Ezeiruaku’s second ejection has become a bigger concern?Schottenheimer had already dealt with Ezeiruaku after his earlier ejection. The Cowboys coach again addressed the young defender after the Saints practice and stressed that Ezeiruaku cannot hurt the team by losing his composure.Speaking after the practice, Schottenheimer called Ezeiruaku a “very bright young man” and said he understands that he cannot hurt the football team. The coach also described the incident as part of a “growth mindset” and said Dallas has leaders who can help him improve.The message from Schottenheimer and Jones is similar. Dallas does not want to remove Ezeiruaku’s aggression. The Cowboys want him to know when that aggression has gone too far.That is especially important because Ezeiruaku has a meaningful role to play on the Dallas defense. He started nine games as a rookie and recorded two sacks, giving the Cowboys reason to continue developing him as part of their pass rush.The Cowboys therefore have no reason to give up on him over a pair of training-camp incidents. But they also cannot ignore repeated punches, especially when the latest incident helped turn a joint practice into a league disciplinary issue.The NFL fined Dallas and New Orleans $500,000 each after reviewing the fights. The league reminded teams that they must prevent unsportsmanlike behavior at joint practices, particularly conduct that could cause injuries.Jones called Dallas’ fine “pretty stiff” and said the Cowboys will appeal. He still understands why the league wants teams to control these situations.That creates two separate consequences for Ezeiruaku’s team. The Cowboys will challenge the $500,000 organizational fine, while Ezeiruaku and other players involved will pay separate fines to Dallas.The Cowboys have not revealed Ezeiruaku’s exact penalty. For now, Jones has made the main point clear: the linebacker will face a financial consequence, and the team expects him to learn from it.For Ezeiruaku, the next step is on the field. The Cowboys still want his physical style and pass-rush ability. They simply need him to keep his punches out of the equation.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Will Mike Evans play in week 1? What the latest update means for the 49ers star WR
articles.summary: Mike Evans’ latest injury has added another concern to a San Francisco 49ers roster already dealing with several health issues.
articles.body: Mike Evans’ latest injury has added another concern to a San Francisco 49ers roster already dealing with several health issues. The veteran wide receiver first missed time with a quad strain earlier this month, then returned for a joint practice before leaving another session with his left quad wrapped in ice. That naturally raised questions about his availability for Week 1 against the Los Angeles Rams. Still, the latest comments from Kyle Shanahan and reports from the 49ers beat suggest the team is not overly worried about the issue.Will Mike Evans play in Week 1?There is no certainty as of now, but there is still hope. For now, there is more reason for optimism than concern surrounding Evans. The 49ers signed the six-time Pro Bowler to a three-year, $42.4 million contract after his 12 seasons with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, expecting him to become an important part of their passing attack.His transition to Kyle Shanahan’s offense has not been completely smooth, though. Evans suffered a quad strain on August 3 and missed several practices before returning for San Francisco’s joint session with the Tennessee Titans on August 11.The bigger concern came a week later. During the 49ers’ joint practice with the Los Angeles Chargers ahead of their second preseason game, Evans was pulled from the session and had his left quad reportedly treated with ice. There was no clear indication of a new injury or exactly what caused the discomfort.San Francisco beat reporter Matt Maiocco offered some relief, reporting, “Kyle Shanahan said Mike Evans was just experiencing some tightness. He does not think it’s anything serious.”ESPN NFL reporter Nick Wagoner also suggested there was little immediate reason for alarm, saying Shanahan “didn’t sound concerned, nor did it look particularly painful for Evans, but we’ll see where he is when the team returns to practice this weekend. Hard to imagine he will play (or would have) on Thursday night.”That approach makes sense for a veteran receiver who has already missed significant time. Evans appeared in only eight games last season because of injuries, making his health an important part of San Francisco’s plans.The 49ers do have alternatives. De’Zhaun Stribling has impressed during training camp and the preseason, while Deebo Samuel Sr. and Demarcus Robinson remain part of the receiver group. Christian Kirk is also dealing with an injury, however, which makes Evans’ availability even more valuable.For now, the expectation is that Evans should be ready for Week 1, provided the quad responds well when the 49ers return to practice. San Francisco will likely avoid pushing him unnecessarily in the preseason. The real test will come when the team begins preparing specifically for the Rams and Evans’ status becomes clearer.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NFL week 10 results: San Francisco 49ers, Kansas City Chiefs and Cincinnati Bengals win
articles.summary: The NFL's brightest stars lit up week 10 of the 2026 season with some astonishing plays as the San Francisco 49ers, Kansas City Chiefs and Cincinnati Bengals all won on Sunday.
articles.body:
The NFL's brightest stars lit up week 10 of the 2026 season with some astonishing plays on Sunday.

The likes of Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey, Patrick Mahomes, Jahmyr Gibbs and Ja'Marr Chase showcased their skills with some explosive action to help their teams to victory.

The San Francisco 49ers produced a historic display in Dallas while there were also big wins for the Kansas City Chiefs, Detroit Lions and Cincinnati Bengals.

It means the 49ers and Buffalo Bills continue to share the league's best record (8-1), while five teams moved to 7-2, including the in-form Jacksonville Jaguars.

The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys have a fierce rivalry stretching back to the 1990s and they delivered another classic with a shootout in Texas.

Brock Purdy showed why he is among the leading contenders for the Most Valuable Player award as the 49ers won 46-40, racking up 584 yards of offence - the most Dallas have ever allowed at home.

San Francisco had three touchdowns of more than 65 yards, while Purdy threw for a career-high 389 yards and three touchdowns. The quarterback even blocked for one of the 49ers' other three scores, a 70-yard run by Deebo Samuel on a reverse trick play.

The highlights were two Purdy passes to Christian McCaffrey. The first saw Purdy show remarkable poise as he scrambled out of the pocket before finding McCaffrey for a 74-yard score, while the second was a perfectly-executed play over the middle that saw McCaffrey sprint in untouched from 66 yards.

Dual-threat running back McCaffrey finished with three scores and 223 total yards, including a career-high 161 receiving yards.

Purdy's MVP rival Josh Allen had a relatively quiet game as the Buffalo Bills won 31-12 at the New York Jets, while the Jacksonville Jaguars won 40-23 at the Tennessee Titans.

Including the end of last season, the Jaguars have won 15 of their past 17 regular-season games and must be considered Super Bowl contenders, especially after bringing in three key defensive players before the trade deadline on Tuesday.

Joe Burrow became the new MVP favourite last week and continued his superb form as the Cincinnati Bengals romped to a 38-18 win in their divisional match-up against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

New Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino was among the crowd as Burrow was involved in four touchdowns for the fifth straight game, tying an NFL record.

The Bengals quarterback had 300 passing yards before half-time and finished with 409. Most of them were to Ja'Marr Chase, who claimed 231 yards from just 11 catches for the 7-2 Bengals.

Their divisional rivals, the Cleveland Browns, pulled off another comeback as they recovered from 17-0 down to beat the Houston Texans 27-24.

The Browns have won their opening four home games for the first time since 1963 and are now 6-4.

Quarterback Deshaun Watson led the Browns to a game-winning drive in the fourth quarter of all six of those wins and he said this one was "definitely special" as it came against his former team.

Munich staged the penultimate international game of the season and just playing in Germany was a "dream come true" for the Detroit Lions' wide receiver Amon-Ra St Brown.

The 27-year-old's mother is German, and he and his two brothers speak the language fluently and have been regular visitors to their mother's homeland.

St Brown, who arrived wearing lederhosen and waved the German flag as he ran on to the field, scored two touchdowns as the Lions charged to a 35-10 win over the New England Patriots.

Yet St Brown was outshone by team-mate Jahmyr Gibbs, who had 99 receiving yards, 153 rushing yards and two touchdowns, taking him to 62 overall - a new NFL record in a player's first four seasons.

The Patriots lost Drake Maye to an ankle injury when he was sacked on the game's opening drive by Aidan Hutchinson, who injured his knee as he celebrated, and the Lions fear it is a significant injury.

Detroit, the Minnesota Vikings and Chicago Bears are now all 7-2 in the ultra-competitive NFC North, with the Vikings bouncing back after suffering back-to-back defeats.

Kirk Cousins returned to Minnesota before the trade deadline on Tuesday and the veteran quarterback led them to a 30-10 win at their other divisional rival, the 6-4 Green Bay Packers, with their defence claiming eight sacks - the most in a single game this season.

The Las Vegas Raiders allowed Cousins to rejoin Minnesota as they felt Fernando Mendoza, this year's first overall draft pick, was ready to become their starting quarterback.

Mendoza's first start came against the Seattle Seahawks, the Super Bowl champions, and he managed to run in a 10-yard touchdown on the Raiders' opening drive.

But the Raiders' offence then struggled and Mendoza was sacked six times as the Seahawks won 21-13.

"It's good to get punched in the face because now it's a great opportunity to grow and learn," said Mendoza.

Seattle quarterback Drew Lock made two big touchdown passes on the run, one to Cooper Kupp and the other a 71-yard score by Jaxon Smith-Njigba.

How mum's struggle inspired Mendoza's rise to top NFL draft pick

The Kansas City Chiefs' run game has caught the eye so far this season, in particular new signing Kenneth Walker, but he was out injured on Sunday as Patrick Mahomes reminded everyone he has one of the best arms in the business.

For the first time since 2022, the three-time Super Bowl winner threw for five touchdowns, plus 348 yards, as Kansas City won 35-13 at the Atlanta Falcons.

Running back Emmett Johnson stepped up in the absence of Walker to claim 101 rushing yards, 70 receiving yards and two touchdowns.

Mahomes made explosive plays to Cyrus Allen and Andrew Armstrong for their first NFL scores, while fellow wide receiver Josh Downs scored on his debut after the Chiefs traded for him on deadline day.

That took Mahomes to 332 career touchdown passes, including the play-offs, putting the 31-year-old top of the all-time list for the most in a player's first 10 seasons.

The Chiefs are 7-2 and will need their receiving corps to ease the burden on Walker during a tough five-game stretch after next week.

articles.title: Dianna Russini's post-scandal comeback was no accident as she carefully planned her return to earn respect
articles.summary: Dianna Russini is back on air, and by most accounts she planned every step.
articles.body: Dianna Russini is back on air, and by most accounts she planned every step. The former NFL insider returned to sports media on November 11, 2026, nearly seven months after Page Six published photos of her with Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel at an Arizona resort. Both denied any wrongdoing, though more photos and videos kept surfacing, and Russini eventually resigned from The Athletic. Her new show, The Russini Report, airs through a partnership with offshore sportsbook BetUS. A source now says advisers shaped the whole plan, down to the role she would take and how she would talk about the scandal.Dianna Russini planned her comeback for months after the Mike Vrabel scandalPage Six quotes a source who says Russini worked on this return for a long time. Her advisers pushed her toward commentary instead of going back to scoop-driven reporting. The source said:“Advisers close to Russini were quite suggestive that coming back in the role of commentator is a smarter long-term and short-term decision than coming back as an insider.”The idea was to make her a voice, not an insider. Advisers told her, in the source’s words, “If she’s going to go back to football, navigate her into a role where she’s going to be respected.”The Russini Report is only the first step, according to the source. Other projects are waiting, and she is in the process of taking a couple of them.The BetUS deal is the part that confuses people. The sportsbook has a controversial reputation and is not allowed to operate in the US. The source argued the partnership gave Russini room to “create and craft the program that she wanted to make.”Russini addresses the Vrabel scandal in her premiereThe premiere did not start smoothly. The one-hour episode ran almost an hour late because the site needed to add capacity. BetUS posted:“Well… you broke it. The premiere of The Russini Report drew a record-breaking audience today! We’re adding more seats so everyone gets in. Stay with us! We’ll be back shortly.”When the show finally went live, Russini spoke about the scandal without naming Vrabel. She said she had plenty of time to think about who she wants to be. She also said she held long conversations with people tied to football, and many gave her honest advice.In her own words:“Over the last few months, I have had a lot of time to think about my life and my priorities and the person I want to be moving forward and being home in New Jersey with my husband and our two little boys and being truly present.”The answer leaned on family, not football, and left Vrabel’s name out entirely. That looks deliberate, and it fits the advice her team reportedly gave her. Whether viewers accept it is another question. The premiere crowd came out of curiosity, and curiosity fades fast. Week two is the real test.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NFL Week 10: A San Francisco score fest and two big injuries
articles.summary: Week 10 of the NFL season featured a San Francisco score fest, a costly clash in Germany and three quarterbacks making their first career starts.
articles.body: Week 10 of the NFL season featured a San Francisco score fest, a costly clash in Germany and three quarterbacks making their first career starts. Here’s everything you need to know from Sunday. Can anyone stop the 49ers? On paper, the sieve-like Dallas Cowboys defense going up against the San Francisco 49ers’ offense looked like a mismatch. On the field, it played out the same way — although the Cowboys kept it interesting by scoring plenty themselves. San Francisco improved to 8-1 on the season with the 46-40 road victory, in which Kyle Shanahan’s offense ran 62 plays and gained 584 yards. That average of 9.4 yards per play was the highest of any offense of the last two years, according to NFL research. And that’s even counting the five sacks the 49ers took for a loss of 19 yards. Three touchdowns went for 66 yards or longer. Could Brock Purdy be building a case for MVP? With three more touchdowns Sunday, he now has 22 touchdowns against five turnovers this season, all while missing multiple teammates on offense due to injuries. For his career, Purdy is 4-0 against Dallas, with nine touchdowns against zero turnovers. He also threw a downfield block to aid a long touchdown run. The Cowboys (4-6) have now allowed 20-plus points in 17 consecutive games, the longest active streak in the league. They continue to trail the New York Giants in the NFC East. Big injuries for the Lions and Patriots The Lions got Sunday started with a 35-10 win over the Pats in Germany, but the blowout was marred by key injuries for both sides. New England quarterback Drake Maye left in the first quarter with an ankle injury after he was sacked by Detroit defensive end Aidan Hutchinson — who also hurt himself on the same play. Hutchinson leapt in celebration after the sack, and his right knee buckled as he hit the turf. Both injuries are believed to be “significant,” NFL Network reports, raising question marks about two teams with Super Bowl aspirations. Another Browns win, another Deshaun Watson comeback The Browns improved to 6-4 Sunday, as quarterback Deshaun Watson led yet another last-minute win. In each of Cleveland’s six wins this season, Watson has led a game-winning drive, including four fourth-quarter comebacks. The Texans led 17-0 in this one, only for the Browns to finish the game on a 27-7 run. Watson completed 25 of 40 passes for 312 yards, with no touchdowns and one interception. He owes a debt of gratitude to his defense, which held Houston to a whopping six three-and-outs in the second half. Watson led a short, three-play drive to put Cleveland ahead with under a minute to go. The biggest play of the game was a 30-yard connection between Watson and tight end Harold Fannin Jr., which set up the go-ahead touchdown run by Quinshon Judkins. With the win, the Browns are now 4-0 at home for the first time since 1963 and remain very much in the hunt in the AFC North. Bengals win critical AFC North matchup The Browns weren’t the only big winners in their division Sunday. The NFC North has earned headlines all season because of how difficult the competition is, but don’t overlook the competition taking place in the AFC North, too. Cincinnati’s 38-18 win on “Sunday Night Football” improved it to 7-2 while dropping Pittsburgh to 6-3. Cleveland is lurking, at 6-4, while Baltimore is 4-5. The win was critical for the Bengals because they had already lost once to the Steelers, in Week 3. And the 49ers’ Purdy has competition in the MVP debate, because Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is on an historic tear after throwing for 409 yards and four touchdowns. He has now scored four or more touchdowns in five consecutive games, tied with Peyton Manning in 2004 for the longest streak in NFL history. Speaking of Burrow, how ridiculous was it that 231 of his passing yards went to star receiver Ja’Marr Chase alone? The eight Steelers who caught a pass Sunday combined for 143 receiving yards total. Mahomes moves past Manning The record set Sunday by Kansas City quarterback Patrick Mahomes was a decade in the making. Mahomes threw five touchdown passes in a 35-13 Chiefs (7-2) win over Atlanta (3-7) and now has thrown for more touchdown passes than any quarterback in NFL history through their first 10 seasons. That record had belonged to Peyton Manning, with 327. Mahomes entered Sunday tied with Manning’s mark, before quickly passing it during a game in which he lit up the Falcons even though running back Kenneth Walker Jr. didn’t play (groin) and tight end Travis Kelce injured his right ankle early in the opening quarter. This was the record-setting throw: It was Mahomes’ first five-touchdown game since Week 1 of 2022. Somebody has to win the NFC South The Panthers beat the Saints 20-17 on a walk-off field goal in New Orleans. Carolina is 4-5 after the victory…and in sole possession of first place in the NFC South. The Panthers won the division last year with a losing record of 8-9. QB carousel If you’ve had the feeling you’ve seen more quarterbacks play this season than is typical, your instinct is correct. With No. 1 overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza taking over in Las Vegas, Carson Beck starting in Arizona and Kyle McCord starting Sunday for Miami, it marked only the second time in the last 15 years that 50 or more quarterbacks had started a game through Week 10 (with 2019 being the other instance). Mendoza started strong but ultimately struggled against the defending champion Seattle Seahawks. He ran for a touchdown on the Raiders’ opening drive, but he finished the game with only 143 yards on 17-of-29 passing in a 21-13 loss. Mendoza was also sacked six times, though he did pick up 22 yards on the ground. Since the 1970 merger, quarterbacks selected No. 1 overall have now gone 5-24-1 in their first career start. Beck had a rough day, completing 11 of 18 throws for 108 yards. He was picked off twice and sacked five times in a 34-6 defeat to the Rams. McCord completed 17 of 32 passes for 209 yards in a 24-22 Dolphins loss to Indianapolis. The only Dolphins passing touchdown of the day, however, was thrown by receiver Malik Washington as part of a trick play. Trade deadline’s big move pays dividends Making his first start for the Vikings since 2023, Kirk Cousins led Minnesota to a 30-10 victory over the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. Cousins was acquired just five days prior from the Las Vegas Raiders, and he combined with another dominant Vikings defensive display to end Minnesota’s two-game losing streak and improve the team’s record to 7-2. The performance made clear why so many tipped the Vikings as contenders if they could only marry their defensive prowess with competent quarterback play. The Vikings are now two games clear of Green Bay, keeping pace with Detroit and the Chicago Bears in the loaded NFC North. Aaron Donald earns first sack in 1,050 days Since he unretired and rejoined the Rams before the season, Aaron Donald had yet to truly look like the three-time former NFL defensive player of the year. Sure, the defensive lineman had affected opposing offenses in hard-to-measure ways by forcing them to account for him, but he’d yet to record a sack. Until Sunday. In his eighth game of his return, Donald sacked Beck, the Arizona rookie, to record his first sack in 1,050 days. He added to his total later with a half-sack. The Rams (6-4) won their fourth straight game by smothering the Cardinals (3-7) all game in a 34-6 win so lopsided the Rams ran more than twice as many plays. It marked Arizona’s franchise-record 11th consecutive loss at home.

articles.title: Why the Chiefs can’t afford to lose Travis Kelce down the stretch: A scary ankle moment in Atlanta reminds Kansas City how much it leans on its veteran tight end
articles.summary: Travis Kelce went to the locker room after the Chiefs’ first drive in Atlanta on Sunday, and there was real concern about his ankle.
articles.body: Travis Kelce went to the locker room after the Chiefs’ first drive in Atlanta on Sunday, and there was real concern about his ankle. He had just caught a 23-yard pass on the opening play, then had his ankle stepped on and needed it retaped. He returned, finished with two catches for 30 yards, and Kansas City beat the Falcons 35-13 to move to 7-2. The scare still matters. It was the same ankle that bothered him four weeks ago, and the Chiefs now play three games in 12 days.Why Travis Kelce remains hard to replace in the Chiefs’ offenseTravis Kelce is 37 now, and his numbers are not what they were in his prime. That does not change what he gives Patrick Mahomes. He is the outlet when a play breaks down and the target Mahomes trusts on a long third down. He turned Sunday’s opening snap into a 23-yard gain, which shows how fast Mahomes goes to him.Sunday also showed the other side of it. Tight end Jared Wiley hurt his right ankle and was ruled out, which left Kansas City thin at the position. The offense barely noticed. Mahomes threw five touchdown passes and finished with 348 yards. Emmett Johnson ran for 101 yards and caught two scores. Atlanta also gave the ball away twice, and the Chiefs never did.The defense did its part too. Kansas City sacked Atlanta three times, intercepted a pass and broke up nine throws. Atlanta got a successful onside kick and two late scores, but the game was settled by then.That is the fair counterpoint, and it is a good one. This offense can work without Kelce for stretches. But the Falcons will not be the defense Kansas City sees in January. Playoff teams squeeze the middle of the field, and Kelce still finds room there after close to a decade of reps with Mahomes. A tight end who can read a zone and sit down in it is hard to coach into a young roster. Younger receivers are learning that language. Kelce already speaks it.What the next three games mean for his ankleThe schedule is not kind to a sore ankle. The Chiefs host Arizona on Sunday, play at Buffalo on Thanksgiving night, then visit the Rams on Thursday, Dec. 3. Buffalo comes just four days after Arizona. Kelce also came into Sunday as a full participant in all three practices with no injury tag, so this was not something the team was managing on paper.He hurt the same ankle against the Chargers in Week 6 and came back from that one too. Twice in four weeks, he has gotten up and gone back to work. That says plenty about his toughness. It also leaves the Chiefs with a question they have to answer honestly: how many more times should he do that?Arizona looks like the right place to be careful. After losing at Seattle and Denver in back-to-back weeks, the Chiefs have beaten the Jets and Falcons by a combined 45 points, and one win-probability model gives them a 92.7 percent chance against the Cardinals. If Kelce is limited in practice this week, there is little reason to rush him. Buffalo is a different game, on a short week, and the Chiefs will want him fresh for it.So the first thing to watch is Wednesday’s practice report, and the second is whether Kelce is out there at all.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body:
New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye reportedly suffered a "significant" ankle injury against the Detroit Lions on Sunday that kept him in Germany, and there is concern he may be ruled out for the remainder of the season, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said he "wouldn't imagine him being available coming out of the bye."

Maye was seen going to the locker room with an apparent limp during the first quarter:

Maye has started all 10 games for the Patriots this season after starting all 17 during the team's 2025 campaign. He also started all four playoff games during the team's run to the last Super Bowl.

The No. 3 overall pick of the 2024 NFL draft has been fairly durable throughout the early portion of his career, which is one reason he reached the Pro Bowl in each of his first two seasons.

However, this setback meant New England had to turn toward Tommy DeVito under center against a formidable Lions team that entered play with a 6-2 record.

Maye has had something of an up-and-down 2026 season, as he completed 65.4 percent of his passes for 2,282 yards and 18 touchdowns in his first nine games. Yet he also entered Sunday's matchup leading the NFL with 11 interceptions.

Three of those picks came in the last game against the Green Bay Packers, so he was surely looking to bounce back Sunday against the Lions.

The timing of the injury is particularly concerning for New England, as it dropped three of its last four games to fall to 5-5 on the season and eighth in the AFC standings.

A prolonged absence for Maye would put the reigning AFC champion's playoff chances in serious doubt.

articles.title: 49ers' Fred Warner Hypes Brock Purdy After Win vs. Cowboys, 'I Promise He's the MVP' of the NFL
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers linebacker Fred Warner made a bold proclamation about teammate Brock Purdy following Sunday's 46-40 win over the Dallas Cowboys.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers linebacker Fred Warner made a bold proclamation about teammate Brock Purdy following Sunday's 46-40 win over the Dallas Cowboys.

"I promise he's the MVP of our league," Warner said, per ESPN's Nick Wagoner . "He's the best quarterback, and I'm glad that he's on our side."

Purdy went 22-of-28 for 389 yards and three touchdowns, and his 154.5 passer rating fell just short of perfection (158.3).

Defense was optional at AT&T Stadium as the 49ers and Cowboys combined for 1,023 yards. San Francisco had three scoring plays go more than 65 yards, which Wagoner noted was the first time it had happened since the St. Louis Rams pulled it off in 2000.

For Purdy, his performance added to what's his best season since his 2023 breakout. He has thrown for 2,369 yards, 20 touchdowns and five interceptions, and his 81.4 QBR is second only to the Cincinnati Bengals' Joe Burrow.

Purdy was fourth in the 2023 MVP voting, and he has the third-best odds (+400) at FanDuel Sportsbook . Some may disagree with Warner's remark, but the 26-year-old signal-caller is at least a contender for the honor.

Whether or not he wins the MVP, Purdy's production is a strong response to his critics who have questioned whether 2023 was a bit of an aberration. He's displaying why the Niners signed him to a $265 million extension last year.

If Purdy keeps this up, San Francisco might finally be able to lift the Super Bowl title that has proven so elusive for coach Kyle Shanahan.

Still, the Lions star is on pace for a record-setting campaign. He has run for 1,000 yards and 11 touchdowns while catching 41 passes for 384 yards and two scores. If Gibbs can maintain his average of 153.8 yards from scrimmage per game, he'll break Chris Johnson's all-time record (2,509 yards) from 2009.

Gibbs is a narrow favorite for Offensive Player of the Year at +105, ahead of Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba at +145. That's obviously a much more attainable award.

articles.title: Drake Maye reportedly could miss remainder of season with 'significant lower leg injury,' Pats fear ankle fracture
articles.summary: Drake Maye was injured after an Aidan Hutchinson sack.
articles.body:
New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye reportedly could potentially miss the remainder of the season with what is described as a "significant lower-leg injury," NFL Network reported early Monday.

The Patriots reportedly fear Maye could be dealing with a fractured ankle, per ESPN.

Maye did not travel with the team to the United States after the contest, instead staying in Germany to undergo additional testing. The injury could require surgery and Maye is looking at a lengthy absence, if not a season-ending one.

Maye was knocked out of Sunday's loss against the Detroit Lions in Munich following the team's first offensive drive. Maye, who was sacked to end the drive, appeared to sustain an ankle injury on the play. When the Patriots took the field for their second offensive drive of the day, Maye went to the locker room.

He was replaced by backup Tommy DeVito, who finished 12-for-24 passing for 81 yards, 1 touchdown and 1 interception. He was sacked four times in Detroit's 35-10 victory .

The Patriots (5-5) quickly ruled Maye as questionable to return due to an ankle injury. He was eventually ruled out for the contest.

New England has a bye next week before facing the Los Angeles Chargers on Nov. 29.

Maye wasn't the only player injured on the play. Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson, who sacked Maye on the play, sustained a knee injury after celebrating the sack . He walked off the field under his own power and visited the blue medical tent on the sideline before walking to the locker room. Hutchinson was later ruled out.

articles.title: NFL Monday Night Football preview: Ravens look to stay relevant with Jacoby Brissett, Chargers look for a win
articles.summary: Jacoby Brissett will make his first start of the season for the Ravens.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens would have been excused for packing it up this season and not trading off draft picks for a long shot on a discarded quarterback dragging them to the playoffs.

But the Ravens haven't quit on the season. They traded a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick to the Arizona Cardinals for Jacoby Brissett and a 2027 fifth-round pick. Brissett will make his first start with the Ravens, who have quarterbacks Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley on injured reserve, on Monday night.

Nothing can save the Los Angeles Chargers' season. It has been over for weeks. But they do want to get a win before the 0-17 questions start.

It's not a marquee Monday night matchup, but both teams have something to play for.

The Ravens are 4-5 and technically still in the AFC wild-card race. The dream for the Ravens is for Brissett, who started eight games for the Cardinals this season before being traded, to keep the team in the race until Jackson can return. The team said Jackson is out six-to-10 weeks with a dislocated right thumb. If Jackson returns at the shortest end of that timeline he could be back Week 16. That would give Baltimore three regular-season games and the playoffs, though there's a lot of work to do to be relevant when Jackson returns.

The Chargers will try to play spoiler. They are 0-8 and everything has gone wrong. Before this season, Justin Herbert has been one of the NFL's better quarterbacks, but this season he has six touchdowns and 11 interceptions. New offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel hasn't worked out. The defense ranks 28th in points allowed. It has been a nightmare of a season and isn't even half over.

The Chargers are just looking for their first win of the season, long after every other NFL team got one. The Ravens hope it's not at their expense.

An 0-8 team is long out of the playoff mix, but don't underestimate the desire to get one win on the board. Nobody remembers the one-win teams in NFL history, while everyone will remember the winless ones forever. Nobody wants to join that group, including the 2026 Chargers. But the Chargers have more than a half of a season to get one win. The Ravens are favored and can get back to 5-5 with a win. While it would still be hard to figure out how the Ravens can get to the playoffs even if they get back to .500, at least they'd have a chance. That means they need it more, though don't underestimate how badly teams want to change that zero in the win column this deep into the season.

Brissett is the key figure in Monday night's game. It's rare for quarterbacks who can step in and start to be available, but the Cardinals were ready for a change. Brissett was benched in a game against the Cowboys, Gardner Minshew II led a comeback win and Brissett was demoted to third string behind Minshew (who suffered a season-ending injury in Week 9) and rookie Carson Beck. Part of why it's hard to imagine Brissett being good enough to keep the Ravens relevant is that he was benched by a 3-7 team and the Cardinals were 4-16 in his starts the past two seasons. But he was better than any other realistic option, and can at least deliver the ball to playmakers like Zay Flowers and make teams respect the passing game, which can open things up for Derrick Henry.

This is a game that looked much better on paper in August. Just how bad have the Chargers — the only winless team both against the spread (0-7-1) and straight up (0-8) — been this season? This game was Ravens -2.5 in the offseason, and is now Ravens -4.5 … despite Los Angeles having its starting QB in Justin Herbert and Baltimore starting a QB (Jacoby Brissett) that it traded for less than two weeks ago. The Chargers have too much talent to keep losing every game. I think at least their winless streak, at least against the number, ends here. — Ben Fawkes

Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub .

Scoring expectations are modest as the Chargers and Ravens finish up Week 10; the total is a cautious 39. Here are three fantasy themes to track as you watch the game.

1. Can Jacoby Brissett get Zay Flowers going? We saw last year that Flowers could still excel without Lamar Jackson — Flowers maintained steady fantasy value even with backup Tyler Huntley. Baltimore knew it had to do something after losing Jackson and Huntley this year, and while Brissett is a journeyman QB, he did support a fantasy-relevant offense in Arizona last year.

2. Will the Chargers find anything that works on offense? While the LAC defense has middle-of-the-pack metrics, the offense is dead last in offensive EPA. Fantasy managers likely have written off Justin Herbert for the year, but they'd like to leave the light on for one of the running backs.

3. What's left in the Derrick Henry tank? Henry has famously defied normal aging expectations for several seasons, but he's finally starting to show attrition — he's averaging 3.9 YPC this season in his age-32 year, a 1.3-yard drop from 2025. The injury chaos in the Baltimore offense hasn't helped, but Henry could be closer to a RB2 moving forward.. — Scott Pianowski
