articles.title: NFL: New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye could miss rest of the season with ankle injury suffered against Detroit Lions
articles.summary: The New England Patriots face the prospect of being without quarterback Drake Maye for the rest of the season after he suffered an ankle injury in Sunday's loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany; Maye was replaced by Tommy DeVito at quarterback
articles.body:
Maye was injured on the opening drive of the game in Munich when he was sacked by Lions pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson, who would himself then also suffer a game and potentially season-ending knee injury by landing awkwardly during his post-sack celebration.

Maye limped to the locker room and was replaced by Tommy DeVito for the remainder of the game as the Patriots lost 35-10 to drop to 5-5 on the year.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Monday that the Patriots fear Maye's injury could keep him out for the rest of the campaign, with ESPN's Adam Schefter adding that it is feared to be a fractured ankle.

Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said on Sunday that the team would run more tests upon returning to the United States, with Maye staying in Germany overnight to determine whether he required surgery.

The Patriots offense collapsed in Maye's absence as back-up quarterback Tommy DeVito finished 12 of 24 for 81 yards, one touchdown and an interception.

It comes ahead of a difficult run that will see the Patriots follow a meeting with the winless Los Angeles Chargers by facing the Buffalo Bills, Minnesota Vikings and Kansas City Chiefs in a bid to keep their season alive.

Maye has struggled to hit the MVP-contending heights of last season so far this year, and has gone 181 of 276 passing for 2,330 yards and 18 touchdowns to 11 interceptions.

The Patriots were dealt another blow in the fourth quarter when star wide receiver AJ Brown exited with a hamstring injury having only just returned from a two-game absence with a knee issue.

"He wasn't able to finish. We'll see what the severity of that is once we get back and kind of go from there," Vrabel added.

articles.title: Joe Burrow Joins Tom Brady & Peyton Manning with Ultra Rare Stats, Reacts to MVP Chants in Win
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow put himself into rarefied air with his performance in Sunday's 38-18 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow put himself into rarefied air with his performance in Sunday's 38-18 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers.

The three-time Pro Bowler went 35-of-44 for 409 yards and four touchdowns. He now has 20 touchdown passes over his last five starts, something only Tom Brady and Peyton Manning have pulled off . He's also the second quarterback all time to have five straight games with at least four combined touchdowns through the air and on the ground.

Burrow is the NFL MVP favorite (+100) at FanDuel Sportsbook , and fans at Paycor Stadium were directing MVP chants his way Sunday night. He isn't entertaining that conversation just yet.

"We'll see," he told reporters about when his MVP candidacy will become more serious.

Teammate Ja'Marr Chase was more emphatic.

"It would be impossible to say anyone is playing better," head coach Zac Taylor said, per Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic. "I'm not watching every game, but I bet the people that aren't talking about him aren't watching our games, because if you are, it's really hard to say that he is not the best player on planet Earth."

Burrow is leading the NFL in average passing yards (310.6) and touchdown passes (27). The Bengals' victory also put them a game ahead of the Steelers for first place in the AFC North.

The Bengals defense deserves its share of credit for the team's 7-2 record. Dexter Lawrence II has made a big impact along the defensive line, and the same goes for free-agent signings Boye Mafe and Jonathan Allen.

Cincy's three-year playoff drought is down largely to a mixture of a porous defense and/or injuries to Burrow. Right now, both are trending in the right direction.

"This is why we do it," Burrow said, per Dehner Jr. "For big moments like that — Steelers, Aaron Rodgers, primetime, two 6-2 teams for sole possession of the division (lead). That's what I love to do. That's why I work so hard to put myself in a good position to play in games like that."

If Burrow remains this prolific on a division winner, his MVP case will be difficult to beat.

articles.title: Week 11 Waiver Wire Pickups Highlighted by Kaelon Black, Caleb Douglas, Seth McGowan
articles.summary: Fantasy football managers will want an early start on their waiver wire plans ahead of Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body:
Fantasy football managers will want an early start on their waiver wire plans ahead of Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season.

Managers are approaching a tricky intersection here with options being fairly limited by all of the pickups so far and roster reinforcements being perhaps needed now more than ever.

Week 11 will be the busiest bye week of the entire campaign with six different teams sitting out: the Atlanta Falcons, Cleveland Browns, Green Bay Packers, Los Angeles Rams, New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks. If that wasn't enough, managers must also contend with a growing injury report that now features, among others, the likes of Drake Maye (ankle), Brock Bowers (ankle) and A.J. Brown (hamstring).

Managers will want to be targeted and direct once waivers open. One quick tip before getting started, though. You should probably triple-check Emmett Johnson's availability before considering the players we recommend. He is too rostered for our purposes (70 percent), but he isn't universally taken the way his 171-scrimmage yard, two-touchdown breakout suggests he should be.

Since Johnson will be unavailable for most managers, though, we'll cut off his mention there and use our typical roster-rate cutoff of 50 percent, using roster percentages from FantasyPros .

Kaelon Black, RB, San Francisco 49ers (37% Rostered)

The 49ers have clearly focused on limiting the workload of Christian McCaffrey. Realistically, they may not have had another choice, considering he's a 30-year-old running back coming off of a 450-touch season (playoffs included).

That plan alone helped Kaelon Black find the field as a rookie third-rounder. The fact he is actually making these opportunities count is the reason why he is elevating from a fantasy handcuff into a legitimate consideration for the flex spot.

Black has now seen double-digit touches in three consecutive contests (and nine in the one right before this stretch). He has averaged 65 scrimmage yards over this three-game stretch, which has also included the first two scores of his career.

Black seems to have a defined, consistent role within one of the league's most explosive offenses. His ceiling will be capped a bit as long as McCaffrey is upright, but Black's elevated floor might be the bigger story here.

Caleb Douglas, WR, Miami Dolphins (39% Rostered)

Look, we get it. Exposing yourself to any part of this Dolphins offense feels like asking for trouble. Especially with the unproven Kyle McCord now under center.

That said, even bad offenses put up numbers. And it sure seems like any produced by Miami's passing game could come from Caleb Douglas, the 6'4", 205-pound playmaking rookie.

The Dolphins want them to come from Douglas, at least. He mad his sixth appearance Sunday and saw at least six targets for the fourth time. And he's really only had two duds in those outings, as the other four have featured at least 70 receiving yards (71 on Sunday on only three receptions) or two touchdowns.

If his volume remains this high, he can be at least a viable spot starter. And if he can become more consistent with his efficiency (22 receptions on 36 targets), he has a possible path to becoming a weekly lineup lock.

Seth McGowan, RB, Indianapolis Colts (19% Rostered)

As the Colts wind down what's already a lost season, they won't run Jonathan Taylor into the ground. That means things are looking up for rookie seventh-rounder Seth McGowan, even if he stopped short of the huge opportunity boost that would've come his way had Indy included Taylor in its trade-deadline subtractions.

McGowan just saw double-digit carries for the second time in his last four outings. And the way he handled them suggests even more should come his way.

He ran for a career-high 77 yards and scored his second touchdown in as many weeks. He has also now produced at least one double-digit run in seven consecutive contests.

The Colts should use this final stretch to figure out exactly what they have in McGowan. Because if he looks the part of a future starter, that rebuild-boosting Taylor trade idea might be worth revisiting over the offseason.

articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers was "not happy" with his team's offensive showing in Sunday's 38-18 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers was "not happy" with his team's offensive showing in Sunday's 38-18 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals.

"Started really slow, couldn't get anything going until the fourth quarter," he said in his postgame press conference. "So that's disappointing."

Rodgers also reflected that the Steelers "shot ourselves in the foot with a couple of plays" and failed to build any early momentum.

Tomlin Says 'We' When Talking Steelers 😅

As frustrated as he might be, the four-time MVP didn't want to overreact about the significance of the result. Peaks and valleys are inevitable across a long season.

The fanbase may feel a little differently because the manner of the defeat reinforced so many existing concerns. Rodgers was invisible in the first half as Cincinnati built a 24-3 lead, and the defense had no solution for making Joe Burrow uncomfortable in the pocket.

Rodgers' mindset after the game was the correct one from a player standpoint. Nothing will be achieved by panicking and publicly throwing teammates or coaches under the bus.

At the same time, Sunday did look like a reality check for a squad that was 6-2 entering Week 10.

Pittsburgh is leaning on a 42-year-old starting quarterback who's past his prime. Its two highest-paid players, T.J. Watt and DK Metcalf, aren't playing up to their contracts. The pass defense, which lost Joey Porter Jr. in a midseason trade, is one of the worst in the league.

The Steelers haven't won a playoff game since the 2016 season. Since then, they've largely remained a solid team that gets exposed against tough opponents.

Sunday night provided compelling evidence that Pittsburgh is on the exact same trajectory this year.

articles.title: Mike Tomlin Says 'We' When Reacting to Steelers' Loss to Joe Burrow, Bengals in Viral Video
articles.summary: Mike Tomlin may not coach the Pittsburgh Steelers anymore, but he still feels a personal connection to their results.
articles.body:
Mike Tomlin may not coach the Pittsburgh Steelers anymore, but he still feels a personal connection to their results.

Reacting to the team's 38-18 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, Tomlin used the royal "we" when referring to the Steelers.

"We didn't get enough four-man rush," he said in his role as an analyst for NBC Sports (6:55 mark).

In case it escaped the attention of anyone, Maria Taylor jokingly pressed Tomlin on his use of "we" with his old employer.

Tomlin might be a broadcaster now, but he coached Pittsburgh for 19 seasons. It's no surprise a deflating defeat to a division rival by the Steelers elicited some extra emotion.

articles.title: Joe Burrow’s MVP chances keep growing, but Bengals star has just 3 words for the award conversation
articles.summary: Joe Burrow is giving the Cincinnati Bengals every reason to believe he belongs in the NFL MVP race.
articles.body: Joe Burrow is giving the Cincinnati Bengals every reason to believe he belongs in the NFL MVP race. His latest performance against the Pittsburgh Steelers was another reminder of how much control he has over this offense. Burrow threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns in a 38-18 victory, helping Cincinnati claim its fifth straight win and sole possession of the AFC North lead. Yet, as the crowd at Paycor Stadium began chanting his name in an MVP call, the quarterback had a simple response. “It's Week 10.”Joe Burrow plays down MVP talk after Bengals' win over SteelersJoe Burrow had every reason to enjoy the attention. He completed 35 of 44 passes against Pittsburgh, threw no interceptions and repeatedly found ways to break through a defense that struggled to contain him. It was the kind of performance that strengthens an MVP argument, especially with Cincinnati now sitting at 7-2.The crowd noticed. MVP chants rang out as Burrow walked off the field following another impressive afternoon. But the quarterback was not interested in making the moment about himself.Sports Illustrated's Jay Morrison reported Burrow's three-word response to the growing discussion: “It's Week 10.”There is a practical side to that reaction. The NFL season still has plenty of football left, and individual awards can quickly become a distraction when a team has bigger goals to chase. Burrow has experienced enough highs and setbacks to understand that a strong November does not guarantee anything in January.His focus also reflects where Cincinnati stands right now. The Bengals have won five consecutive games and moved ahead of Pittsburgh in the AFC North. That matters far more to the quarterback than hearing his name attached to an individual award.Bengals QB has a real chance to make MVP historyJoe Burrow's numbers are becoming difficult to overlook. His 409-yard performance against Pittsburgh was not just about putting up big statistics. He controlled the pace, made accurate throws under pressure and kept Cincinnati's offense productive throughout the game.He also received valuable help from his teammates. Chase Brown finished with 83 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns, while Samaje Perine, Dohnte Meyers and Drew Sample also found the end zone. The defense contributed three sacks and kept Aaron Rodgers from finding much rhythm.That balance is important. MVP discussions often focus heavily on quarterback numbers, but Burrow's strongest case could come from leading a team that is winning consistently. Cincinnati is no longer simply trying to keep pace with its division rivals. It has taken control of the race.There is also a piece of franchise history within reach. Burrow could become only the third Bengals player to win the NFL MVP award. Ken Anderson earned the honor in 1981, followed by Boomer Esiason in 1988. No Cincinnati quarterback has won it since.The competition will not be easy. Brock Purdy, Josh Allen and Jordan Love are among the other quarterbacks in the conversation, with Jacksonville's Trevor Lawrence also in the mix.Burrow's immediate challenge is to keep Cincinnati winning. The Bengals travel to face the Washington Commanders in Week 11, another opportunity to strengthen their position. For now, he seems happy to leave the award talk to everyone else. His answer was short, but his message was clear: there is still a long way to go.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Justin Herbert is 'Not An Instinctive Football Player,' Says NFL Exec amid Chargers' Losing Streak
articles.summary: Before leading the 0-8 Los Angeles Chargers into Monday night's matchup against the Baltimore Ravens, star quarterback Justin Herbert appears to have lost his luster around the league.
articles.body:
Before leading the 0-8 Los Angeles Chargers into Monday night's matchup against the Baltimore Ravens, star quarterback Justin Herbert appears to have lost his luster around the league.

The Athletic's Mike Sando spoke to an executive from another team who highlighted Herbert's regression under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel.

"He's really smart, but he's not an instinctive football player," the exec said of Herbert. "That's what the disconnect is right now. They're asking him to process when that's not his deal. Just give me a play to run, which is what he did in college, which is what he did a little bit when he got to the NFL."

Sando explained how McDaniel's influence has affected Herbert, pointing out that the former Miami Dolphins head coach "imposed a specific system tailored to quick-processing and quick-delivering QBs, whereas his predecessor, Greg Roman, was best known for molding offenses to fit personnel at the position."

Herbert's 11 interceptions are tied for the second-most in the league, and he's completing just 61.3 percent of his passes, the first time in his seven-year career that his completion rate has fallen below 65 percent.

It wasn't long ago that Herbert was viewed as one of the brightest young stars in the NFL. However, his struggles this season have been hard to ignore, as Sando noted that he "is 19th in EPA per pass play out of 21 quarterbacks with at least 20 starts over the past two seasons, including 29th out of 31 qualifying passers this season."

If Herbert's struggles continue, it wouldn't be a surprise if the Chargers' marriage to McDaniel doesn't last long. Los Angeles will try to show that things are moving in a positive direction when it meets Baltimore on Monday Night Football .

articles.title: Jim Everett takes subtle shot at Rams’ former ownership while backing Stan Kroenke after Matthew Stafford’s latest win
articles.summary: Former Los Angeles Rams quarterback Jim Everett believes the team is moving in the right direction under its current ownership, and his latest social
articles.body: Former Los Angeles Rams quarterback Jim Everett believes the team is moving in the right direction under its current ownership, and his latest social media exchange has brought attention to the franchise’s difficult past. After the Rams defeated the Arizona Cardinals 34-6 on November 15, Everett agreed with a fan who compared the team’s present situation with its problems during the old ownership era. His response also brought Stan Kroenke’s leadership into the discussion.Jim Everett reacts to Rams fan’s criticism of Georgia Frontiere’s ownership eraEverett recently responded to a fan on social media who compared the problems he faced during his Rams career with the injury issues Matthew Stafford’s team is dealing with today. The fan pointed out that Everett had struggled without enough support from the team during his playing days, but believed the reason was poor ownership rather than injuries.The fan wrote, “You know how it feels to be without WRs. Except, your situation didn’t have to deal with injuries, it was broke ownership.”Everett agreed that the franchise has made progress under its current setup, replying, “Think the 🐏 are getting it right more than not these days! History is just that. To be learned and moved on.”His words were a clear sign that he sees a difference between the Rams’ past and present. However, Everett did not directly name former owner Georgia Frontiere or accuse her of making specific poor decisions in his reply.Frontiere was the Rams’ principal and majority owner from 1979 until her death in January 2008. During her time with the franchise, the team reached the playoffs three times but did not appear in a Super Bowl. Former team president John Shaw also faced criticism over the way the organization was managed.Everett knows that period well because he played for the Rams from 1986 to 1993. He finished his regular-season career with 23,758 passing yards, a mark that still stands as the franchise record, according to Pro Football Reference and the Pro Football Hall of Fame.Jim Everett’s support for Stan Kroenke comes as Matthew Stafford leads Rams to another winEverett’s positive view of the current Rams setup is not new. In a 2021 interview published on the official Rams website, he openly praised Stan Kroenke for bringing the franchise back to Los Angeles and building SoFi Stadium.“When the Rams came back, if it wasn’t for Stan Kroenke putting $5 billion into that project and building a stadium with his own money, it wasn’t going to happen in California. So I think we’re blessed with Mr. Kroenke, for sure,” Everett said.Kroenke became the Rams’ majority owner in 2010 and later helped bring the franchise back to Los Angeles in 2016. The team also won Super Bowl LVI in February 2022, beating the Cincinnati Bengals 23-20 at SoFi Stadium. These achievements help explain why Everett has spoken positively about the current direction of the organization.Meanwhile, the Rams have continued to show their strength on the field under head coach Sean McVay. On Sunday, Matthew Stafford helped them secure a 34-6 win over the Arizona Cardinals despite missing two of his leading receivers, Puka Nacua and Davante Adams.Stafford completed 18 of 26 passes for 249 yards, three touchdowns and one interception. Nine different players caught passes from him, while Xavier Smith and tight ends Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen helped make up for the missing receivers.The victory gave Los Angeles its fourth consecutive win and improved its record to 6-4. Stafford’s performance also showed how the team can use its other players when its biggest offensive names are unavailable.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: QB Report Cards for 2026 NFL Week 10
articles.summary: New beginnings occur even in the middle of an ongoing NFL season. Case in point, the Minnesota Vikings traded for Kirk Cousins where he rejoined the franchise after leaving in free agency two-and-a-half years ago. Now, the veteran quarterback, who previously spent six season leading the Vikings offense, is exactly who the organization needs as it competes for an NFC North title. Meanwhile, three different rookie quarterbacks made their first career starts during Week 10 action, including this year's No. 1 overall pick, Fernando Mendoza. All three came out on the losing end, yet none of them were completely overwhelmed by their first taste of professional football. Bleacher Report analyzes and grades every single quarterback performance throughout the campaign, because the league's landscape continually changes. Sometimes, it does so more during certain weeks than others.
articles.body:
New beginnings occur even in the middle of an ongoing NFL season. Case in point, the Minnesota Vikings traded for Kirk Cousins where he rejoined the franchise after leaving in free agency two-and-a-half years ago. Now, the veteran quarterback, who previously spent six season leading the Vikings offense, is exactly who the organization needs as it competes for an NFC North title. Meanwhile, three different rookie quarterbacks made their first career starts during Week 10 action, including this year's No. 1 overall pick, Fernando Mendoza. All three came out on the losing end, yet none of them were completely overwhelmed by their first taste of professional football. Bleacher Report analyzes and grades every single quarterback performance throughout the campaign, because the league's landscape continually changes. Sometimes, it does so more during certain weeks than others.

Stat Line : 11 of 18 for 108 yards and two interceptions

Welcome to the NFL, rookie. Enjoy looking across the line of scrimmage to see Aaron Donald and Myles Garret. Oh, good luck trying to outduel the league's reigning MVP, too.

The aforementioned setup was exactly what Carson Beck faced during his first NFL start. It went about as well as expected. To be fair, Beck threw a pair of interceptions and neither one should fall at the feet of the first-year quarterback.

The first pick occurred after the ball bounced out of his receiver's hands once he hit the ground untouched. The second came when the running back ran the wrong route.

"[Beck] did everything we asked him to do," head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters . "I thought he did his job." The Cardinals' schedule won't get easier for the rookie. He simply has to do his best, because an opportunity to move forward as the franchise's QB1 still exists with impressive play during Arizona's final seven games.

Score : 35-13 loss vs. Kansas City Chiefs

Stat Line : 23 of 43 for 286 yards and an interception; four carries for 29 yards

The Atlanta Falcons find themselves in a three-game losing streak. During that span, Michael Penix's owns a one-to-six touchdown-to-interception ratio. The Falcons have scored 20 total points.

The Falcons were particularly awful Sunday during critical downs and working in the red zone. Atlanta finished a combined five for 18 on third and fourth downs. Meanwhile, the Penix-led offense scored one touchdown despite five red-zone trips.

The performance led to a dreaded vote of confidence in Penix from head coach Kevin Stefanski after the contest. However, the possibility of a change at the game's most important position still exists as Atlanta enters its bye week.

"I look at everything every week, don't need a bye week to do those things," Stefanski told reporters . "We need to be better, myself included."

Stat Line : 11 of 21 for 196 yards, one touchdown and an interception; five carries for five yards and two touchdowns

By Josh Allen's standards, the quarterback provided a pedestrian effort against the New York Jets. The previous statement just means he scored three touchdowns in a game where he didn't need to be amazing because the Bills dominated.

Instead, running back James Cook exploded for a season-high 157 rushing yards. Allen best contributions came as a short-yardage runner near the goal line.

Buffalo may be 8-1, but Allen understands his offense can play at a much higher level.

"We feel like there's still so much to learn from and grow from," Allen told reporters . "We're not playing our best football right now, but as we get later into the season, we feel like we're going to get better and learn from these types of moments and these types of games and hopefully start putting it all together soon."

Score : 20-17 win vs. New Orleans Saints

It's how you leave 'em, folks. The Carolina Panthers managed 283 yards of offense Sunday against the New Orleans Saints. The Panthers generated 98 of those yards during their final two offensive possessions, as the team scored 10 points and managed to snatch a victory away from a division opponent.

Obviously, the Panthers benefited greatly from a massive pass interference call during the final drive that placed them into game-winning field-goal range. However, Young took advantage of Chuba Hubbard in the passing game during the previous possession to set up the squad's last touchdown.

"At the end of the day it's one-on-one opportunities," head coach Dave Canales told reporters . "It's Chuba breaking tackles on checkdowns, in the run game, making critical plays because he wants it. That's the type of mentality it's gonna take for us to get to where we want to—a full group with that kind of mentality."

Score : 38-18 win vs. Pittsburgh Steelers

Stat Line : 35 of 44 for 409 yards and four touchdowns

Joe Burrow is doing whatever he wants on a football field regardless of opponent or situation. He's simply seeing the field better than he every has, while placing the ball wherever he wants to throw it.

As a result, Burrow should be the runaway favorite to claim the NFL's 2026 MVP award.

After Sunday night's dismantling of the Pittsburgh Steelers' defense, Burrow now leads qualifying quarterbacks in completion percentage (74.7), passing yards per game (310.6), passing touchdowns (27), QBR (82) and passer rating (117.7). He's reached his final form, which is terrifying for opposing defenses.

"It would be impossible to say anyone is playing better," head coach Zac Taylor told reporters . "I'm not watching every game, but I bet the people that aren't talking about him aren't watching our games, because if you are, it's really hard to say that he is not the best player on planet Earth."

Stat Line : 25 of 40 for 312 yards and an interception; eight carries for 49 yards and a score

The Cleveland Browns famously lack a strong quarterback lineage. However, there was a point in time when that wasn't true.

Between Otto Graham, Frank Ryan and Bernie Kosar, Brian Sipe led the franchise. Sipe emerged as the NFL MVP during the 1980 campaign, while leading the a squad nicknamed the "Kardiac Kids" because its penchant for comeback victories. Deshaun Watson won't be in any conversation regarding the league's most valuable player. Though he's now leading the Kardiac Kids 2.0.

Once again, Cleveland's defense found ways to dictate terms during the second half of a contest and Watson made big plays down the stretch, which allowed the Browns to emerge victorious yet again. The team now has six comeback victories this season, allowing them to be in the playoff race.

"I don't have the end of the story," head coach Todd Monken told reporters . "I just know if our guys keep fighting, keep battling, keep scratching and clawing, they always have a chance."

Score : 46-40 loss vs. San Francisco 49ers

Stat Line : 30 of 51 for 343 yards, five touchdowns and an interception

Dak Prescott has to be sick to his stomach. A quarterback throwing for nearly 350 yards and five touchdowns in one game should be more than enough to produce a decisive victory. Instead, the Dallas Cowboys defense is so consistently bad that Prescott's outstanding play continues to be wasted.

This season, Dallas has scored 30 or more points in six different contests. The team is 3-3 during those games. It's basically a coinflip whether the Cowboys can actually win when their offense is clicking. Furthermore, Dallas is 1-3 when scoring fewer than 30 points.

Brian Schottenheimer's squad only trailed by one point, 17-16, going into Sunday's halftime. The Niners proceeded to score 29 second-half points.

"I thought the second half was unacceptable," Schottenheimer told reporters . "Tackling was atrocious, and we got to do a deep dive on the film and see why. You can't give up three explosive plays of over 65 yards for touchdowns and expect to win in this league."

Score : 35-10 win vs. New England Patriots

Stat Line : 20 of 31 for 303 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions

During Sunday's international affair with the New England Patriots, the Detroit Lions' Jared Goff threw for 300 or more yards for the fourth time this season and at least three touchdowns for the third time. Conversely, the man who opened this season with a chance of breaking the longest interception-less streak has now thrown a pick in three straight games, including two during his latest performance.

Earlier turnovers could even be explained away to some degree. The two Goff threw in Germany were simply poor decisions where the quarterback wasn't able to work around underneath defenders.

However, the Lions' offensive margin of error has increased since the defense has significantly improved in recent weeks.

"The coverage has been tighter just schematically," cornerback Rock-Ya Sin told reporters . "That front seven, they are just ballin, man. Those dudes are unblockable, man. I'm serious. From inside and outside. Whenever you can get those guys humming and then playing tight coverage in the backside. That's a recipe for success."

Score : 30-10 loss vs. Minnesota Vikings

Stat Line : 17 of 27 for 220 yards, one touchdown and an interception

Jordan Love didn't have a chance when facing the Minnesota Vikings' ultra-aggressive defense. Minnesota sacked the Green Bay Packers quarterback eight times Sunday and registered 12 hits in total.

The Packers offense has had issues throughout the year due to a patchwork offensive line, an anemic running game and wide receivers who drop too much passes. The concerns along the front five became more glaring against a defense that knows how to consistently attack and confuse. Plus, Green Bay's offense is predicated on being able to push the ball down the field, which isn't possible when facing constant pressure.

As a result, Green Bay didn't generate much movement, with only 220 yards of offense.

"This is one of those games where they got us," Love told reporters . "They got after us (Sunday), and give them credit, but I think the O-line has been doing a much better job. … We knew what it was going into it: They give people fits, and you gotta be able to overcome (that)."

Stat Line : 20 of 38 for 211 yards, three touchdowns and an interception

If CJ Stroud and the Houston Texans offense provided anything during Sunday's second half, they would have probably escaped Cleveland with a victory. Instead, the Browns roared back from a 17-point halftime deficit, while the Texans managed 52 yards during the second half.

Granted, Houston did score a fourth-quarter touchdown. Otherwise, the Texans provided six second-half three-and-out possessions.

"They've come back on a lot of teams this season and won a lot of games with two-minute drives," Stroud told reporters . "We knew what it was. We were just dead." At 3-6, the Texans better come to life soon or any hope of a postseason berth will quickly fade.

Stat Line : 11 of 22 for 108, one touchdown and tow interceptions

The Indianapolis Colts won for the third time this season, and Daniel Jones did very little to make that possible. Excuses will be made that Alec Pierce is injured and Josh Downs/Keenan Allen are no longer part of the team after being traded. Indianapolis was also down to a pair of backup offensive tackles when Bernhard Raimann suffered a concussion. But the Miami Dolphins are easily one of the league's worst and least talented teams, which helps offset each of those points. Right now, the obvious must be stated: Jones' poor play isn't circumstantial. He's clearly regressed, been far too turnover-prone and his decision-making has been questionable at best. Finally, his command of the Colts' offense is nowhere close to what he showed a year ago. Sometime soon, the Indianapolis coaching staff must make a decision, because Jones has shown he's not the solution. Since the Colts already entered a rebuild, Anthony Richardson should get on the field before the regular season concludes.

Stat Line : 25 of 35 for 352 yards, three touchdowns and an interception; four carries for 27 yards

Trevor Lawrence has rounded into a complete quarterback, particularly from a mental aspect, hence why he now find himself in the MVP conversation.

Lawrence always had the physical ability to play the position at the highest level. But it took time for him to build confidence and a legitimate comfort level within an offensive scheme. He and head coach/offensive play-caller Liam Coen are now simpatico. So far in November, the Jags' signal-caller completed 68 percent of his passes for 804 yards, seven touchdowns and an interception. The turnover came via a tipped pass at the line of scrimmage.

"I just have a lot of comfort in what we're doing, a lot of confidence," Lawrence told reporters. "I know what we're doing. I feel like myself and our whole offense, but myself and the staff, like we're all on the same page. I know what we're trying to get done."

Stat Line : 22 of 35 for 348 yards and five touchdowns

The Kansas City Chiefs offense provided a throwback performance Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons. Instead of a quick dink-and-dunk approach, Patrick Mahomes and Co. once again created chunk plays with regularity and stretched the Falcons defense.

Seven different targets caught passes of 20 or more yards. Mahomes looked like his old, playmaking self daring his opponent to stop the Chiefs whenever he decided to push the ball down the field. He did so after suffering an elbow injury during Kansas City's previous contest.

"Obviously it felt good enough," Mahomes told reporters . "I was a little nervous going into the game, just because it was a little sore. … I didn't feel like in the week of practice I was driving the ball the way I wanted to—some of those deeper in-cut routes and the balls down the field. You don't know until you get out there and that adrenaline starts kicking in a little bit."

Stat Line : 17 of 29 for 143 yards; six carries for 22 yards and a touchdown

The Las Vegas Raiders offense didn't accomplish a lot Sunday against the top-ranked Seattle Seahawks defense. However, the traits that made Fernando Mendoza this year's No. 1 overall draft pick certainly appeared during the rookie's first NFL start.

Mendoza zipped a few nice throws. He extended some plays. Plus, his toughness and calm demeanor allowed him to remain in the moment instead of letting the Seahawks completely fluster the first-time starter.

"It's good to get punched in the face because now it's a great opportunity to grow and learn and to really unveil all the deficiencies that I have in my game, as a future hopeful leader of this offense," Mendoza said after the game .

Raiders fullback Connor Heyward added, "He felt poised, like a veteran quarterback that was ready for the moment," Heyward said. "You wouldn't think he was a rookie out there."

Stat Line : 18 of 26 for 249 yards, three touchdowns and an interception

One of Sean McVay's greatest assets as an NFL head coach is his ability to adapt. The Los Angeles Rams are no longer a team who should unleash quarterback Matthew Stafford and throw it all over the yard. This team's offense now revolves around being able to dictate terms with a physical, downhill rushing attack.

"[Sunday's performance] was a game of, 'We're just going to beat you,'" guard Kevin Dotson told reporters . "'Do what you can. We're not changing our play. You know what's coming. Do it again. Do it again. We might add something in there just to keep you honest, but we're going to do the same thing again.'" Stafford certainly isn't cooked, not after he threw three touchdown passes against a division rival. At the same time, he's not necessarily the offensive focal point anymore. As he ages, the Rams are taking more pressure off the the quarterback position and placing it elsewhere. Meanwhile, Stafford can still flash the player he was last season without having to be that elite performer at all times.

Score : 24-22 loss vs. Indianapolis Colts

Stat Line : 17 of 32 for 209 yards, a fumble lost and a rushing touchdown

The best thing anyone can say about a rookie quarterback in his first start is that he wasn't overwhelmed, especially when expectations are low. The position carries heavy responsibilities at the professional level and it's easy for a young signal-caller to overthink everything instead of just going out and playing. For Kyle McCord, who Miami Dolphins drafted in this year's sixth round, he did enough to help his team win. Unfortunately, three missed kicks by Zane Gonzalez proved to be the difference in the game.

"I thought that he would stay composed," Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley told reporters . "He didn't get rattled. I think it showed—I think it showed in the way he played, in the way he responded—and I'm proud of him." Malik Willis will be on injured reserve for at least three more games. McCord has an opportunity in front of him to impress and possibly take over the position during an obvious evaluation year for the Dolphins' roster.

Stat Line : 21 of 31 for 207 yards, two touchdowns and an interception

Kirk Cousins wasn't spectacular in his return to the Minnesota Vikings, but he provided what the team desperately needed from the quarterback position.

First, Cousins fully understands he must get the ball to wide receiver Justin Jefferson, who set a new season-high Sunday with nine receptions. Second, the Vikings offense, as a whole, played complementary football, while the team's defense continued to dominate.

"His composure, his confidence in the huddle, all of that, it definitely created a positive vibe," Jefferson told reporters . Once again, the Vikings are Cousins' team. At 38, he may not be at the same level he was prior to the Achilles tendon tear that he suffered during the 2023 campaign. But the veteran is going to improve over the next few weeks as he gets more comfortable in his new setup.

New England Patriots: Drake Maye & Tommy DeVito

Stat Line : Maye, three of four for 48 yards; DeVito, 12 of 24 for 81 yards, a touchdown and an interception

Injuries have annihilated any momentum the New England Patriots tried to build this season. Quarterback Drake Maye became the latest casualty.

Maye left Sunday's contest against the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany, due to an ankle injury and didn't return. The exact severity of the injury is not yet known.

"This league isn't always 10-game winning streaks," head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters . "There's adversity in this league … and injuries and everything that you have to deal with. So that's our challenge, and I'm excited to get to work at it. I hope that our guys are because that's what I'm going to try to do.

Tommy DeVito answered the call after Maye went down, but a much-improved Detroit Lions defense didn't make anything easy on the backup quarterback. DeVito led one scoring drive but managed only 81 passing yards and completed only 50 percent of his attempts.

Score : 20-17 loss vs. Carolina Panthers

Stat Line : 25 of 35 for 187 yards, a touchdown, an interception and a fumble lost; six carries for 25 yards

The New Orleans Saints offense is getting healthier and it's nearly at full strength. Even so, the group continues to struggle.

"It was a lack of execution in some of those critical moments for us, as players," Tyler Shough said after the team 's last-second loss to the Carolina Panthers. "... You can't come out of the first half with no points. That was just a lack of details there, on us."

On the positive note, this year's eighth overall draft pick, Jordan Tyson, led the team with 11 receptions for 80s yards. The Saints could possibly show improvement and tangible growth over the next few weeks with Tyson at full tilt and running back Travis Etienne back Jr. back in the lineup.

Score : 24-21 loss vs. Washington Commanders

Stat Line : 23 of 36 for 293 yards, a touchdown and an interception; six carries for 34 yards

The JJ McCarthy may not have opened this season with the New York Giants, but he's making believers within the organization.

"Man, resilience," fellow quarterback Jameis Winston said when asked what McCarthy showed during Thursday Night Football . "He played well. He saw it well. They did some unique things on defense. He found a way to give us a chance to win, and as a quarterback, that's the job." The Giants held a four-quarter lead and New York's defense eventually allowed the Washington Commanders to score the game-winning touchdown with less than a minute to play. Also, the Giants were far two conservative during their two offensive possessions with the lead, which then placed McCarthy in a position where he heaved a pass that was intercepted and put an end to any comeback. Even so, McCarthy continues to make plays. He's performed well enough where the future of the Giants' quarterback position isn't as clear as it was entering the campaign.

New York Jets: Geno Smith & Cade Klubnik

Stat Line : Smith, 13 of 21 for 148 yards; Klubnik, 11 of 20 for 137 yards, an interception and three carries for 26 yards

An injury to Geno Smith may have inadvertently led the New York Jets toward the next phase of the 2026 season. Smith was sandwiched between two Buffalo Bills defenders, suffered an ankle injury and didn't return to the contest.

In Smith's absence, fourth-round rookie Cade Klubnik entered the fray. Klubnik came in firing the football and providing some added athleticism.

"I was actually pretty impressed," running back Breece Hall told reporters , "and even seeing how he was keeping his eyes downfield, seeing how poised he was in the huddle, and commanding the huddle. I was like, 'OK, he's got a lot more to him than what I thought,' especially having to come into this situation that he had to, just not being as prepared as you probably thought he would've been just because he's the No. 2 guy." At 2-8 with Smith nursing an injury, the evaluation of Klubnik should begin.

Entering his final collegiate campus, high expectations were placed on the Clemson product. Klubnik was viewed as a first-round possibility at the time. He and the entire Tigers team disappointed, though, which caused the quarterback to fall in the draft. Still, the upside and growth potential are obvious.

Score : 38-18 loss vs. Cincinnati Bengals

Stat Line : 15 of 29 for 143 yards and two touchdowns

The Pittsburgh Steelers simply had no answers for the Cincinnati Bengals during the second meeting of the season. Pittsburgh lacks explosive options, particularly when a team is able to slow running back Jaylen Warren, as the Bengals did during the primetime contest.

Both of Pittsburgh's scores were meaningless stat-padders will trailing by 28 points in the fourth quarter. Aaron Rodgers no longer has the skill to elevate an offense nor the talent around him to make the most of the situation.

"They played a lot of man coverage," Rodgers told reporters . "We didn't make them pay—at all."

The Steelers' 6-3 record is nothing more than a half-step above mediocrity—which is exactly where this organization has been trapped for the last six seasons.

Stat Line : 22 of 28 for 389 yards and three touchdowns; two carries for 21 yards

If any questions lingered whether Brock Purdy is simply a byproduct of Kyle Shanahan's system or a legitimate top-tier quarterback, those questions have been answered this season. In fact, the Niners accomplished something Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys that they hadn't previously done during Shanahan's tenure.

San Francisco's 584 yards were the most by the team in the last 10 years.

Purdy and his crew accomplished this feat without Mike Evans in the lineup. Deebo Samuel Jr. just returned from injury that forced him to miss a month of action. Plus, Keenan Allen joined the team five days earlier thanks to a pre-deadline trade. The quarterback is making the most of the situation no matter who is around him and even if he needs to block for his teammates.

"The highest compliment I can give anyone on the team is that they are a football player, and Brock is the epitome of that," All-Pro fullback Kyle Juszczyk said of his quarterback . "Whatever he's asked to do, he's going to go do it."

Stat Line : 14 of 17 for 240 yards, two touchdowns and two fumbles lost; six carries for 20 yards

Is Drew Lock a better starting option for the Seattle Seahawks this season when compared to Sam Darnold?

Seattle has now won all four games where Lock played extensively. He did fumble twice against the Las Vegas Raiders, but he's yet to throw an interception. Though one of those turnovers came when his running back accidentally knocked the ball out of the quarterback's hand.

Otherwise, Lock has been more than a typical QB2 this fall.

"I love playing," Lock told reporters . "We'll keep it at that. I love playing. Football's a lot of fun to be out there."

The original question may be posited, but the Seahawks are Darnold's team. Head coach Mike Macdonald isn't going to switch from a Super Bowl-winning quarterback. At the same time, the Seahawks aren't at a disadvantage when Lock's in the lineup. Plus, the 30-year-old signal-caller may be setting himself up to sign as a starter elsewhere next offseason.

Score : 40-23 loss vs. Jacksonville Jaguars

Stat Line : 28 of 39 for 239 yards, two touchdowns and an interception; three carries for 39 yards

The Tennessee Titans defense has played so poorly in recent weeks that improvement by quarterback Cam Ward has been overlooked to a degree.

This entire season has been about Ward's development or lack thereof. When the second-year signal-caller starts to show legitimate signs of life, the Titans have been blown out of the water in back-to-back contests, because their opponents scored a combined 83 points.

Meanwhile, Ward posted his best completion percentage in back-to-back games, threw for 535 yards, ran for 80 more and contributed four touchdowns with only one interception.

"I always think we are getting better each and every week," Ward told reporters . "We are very young, but we don't take that as an excuse. We think we can compete with anybody in the NFL—we are competing what anybody in the NFL, and we just have to continue to try and win games."

Stat Line : 23 of 33 for 249 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions; 11 carries for 28 yards

Jayden Daniels played like a great basketball shooter during Thursday Night Football . He just kept shooting even after two huge mistakes toward the end of the game. Ultimately, Daniels and Stefon Diggs connected and split the New York Giants defense for the game-winning 32-yard touchdown pass.

"I gave a little signal to Stef," Daniels told reporters , "and he went on a slant—and the rest is history."

The play is a microcosm of Daniels' play this season. Injuries have derailed the development of the 2024 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year. Despite the turnovers, Daniels is once again building a comfort level within the Commanders' offense.

"I think I'm starting to get into a rhythm," Daniels said. "It shows the more games you play consistently, the more reps you get, the flow and rhythm. It was tough last year being in and out of the lineup and trying to catch a rhythm. Like, football, you practice more than you play. So you could practice all you want, but it's nothing that could replicate the game."

articles.title: NFL Coach Clowns Kyler Murray, Carson Wentz After Justin Jefferson's Success with Kirk Cousins
articles.summary: One rival NFL coach was blunt in discussing the contrast in the Minnesota Vikings offense before and after the return of quarterback Kirk Cousins.
articles.body:
One rival NFL coach was blunt in discussing the contrast in the Minnesota Vikings offense before and after the return of quarterback Kirk Cousins.

The coach highlighted one sequence in Minnesota's 30-10 win over the Green Bay Packers where Cousins found star wide receiver Justin Jefferson on five straight completions.

"I mean, that is just quality ball right there," the coach told Mike Sando of The Athletic. "Cousins wears the guy out. Jefferson is huffing and puffing. The kid takes himself out of the game. It's like he had fallen out of shape because for two months, he's been watching (Kyler) Murray scramble and (Carson Wentz) bounce it off the ground 5 yards in front of him. It's funny, but it's true."

Cousins went 21-of-31 for 207 yards, two touchdowns and one interception, while Jefferson had nine catches for 74 yards. Neither had a monster performance, but the Vikings offense simply looked sharper than it had in recent weeks.

Cousins' 38-yard touchdown pass to Myles Price in the first quarter was the one play more than any other that illustrated the difference.

"That ball he threw on that 3rd-and-23, that's as good of a Tier 1 throw as you will see in the NFL all year," the coach said to Sando. "There is only one place he can put the ball, but he actually does one better. He back-shoulders it, twisting the receiver to keep him away from the corner.

"You have to be not afraid to make that throw — and remember, he spent two days game-planning for Seattle (while with the Raiders), flew in Tuesday night and had to switch gears."

A different coach alluded to the growing criticism Kevin O'Connell was getting due to the Vikings' inconsistent QB play. He brought out the best in Cousins and helped Sam Darnold resurrect his career, but 2024 first-round pick J.J. McCarthy was a flop, while Murray and Wentz have struggled.

The opposing coach defended O'Connell when it came to Wentz specifically.

"He's a quarterback whisperer, so why can't he get Wentz to play better?" they said. "Because the guy is never playing good. Never."

The Vikings got off to a 6-2 start in spite of their quarterbacks, and their losses to the Detroit Lions and Buffalo Bills led one to believe the formula was no longer sustainable.

Cousins is 38 years old with a major Achilles injury in his past. Maybe the cracks begin to show as the season wears on.

For now, the four-time Pro Bowler is exactly the upgrade the Vikings sought ahead of the NFL trade deadline.

articles.title: New Patriots Rumors on Jimmy Garoppolo, Mike Vrabel's QB1 Plan After Drake Maye's Injury
articles.summary: A reunion between the New England Patriots and Jimmy Garoppolo could be on the table in the wake of Drake Maye's injury.
articles.body:
A reunion between the New England Patriots and Jimmy Garoppolo could be on the table in the wake of Drake Maye's injury.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported Monday that New England is "expected to explore the QB market during the bye week," and Garoppolo is one such solution.

The Patriots need to bolster their depth at the position with ESPN's Adam Schefter reporting Maye will be sidelined indefinitely due to what could be a fractured ankle.

For now, Tommy DeVito is penciled in as the starter for a Week 12 matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers.

With the NFL trade deadline having passed, New England's options to backfill Maye's spot in the depth chart are limited. It says a lot that signing Garoppolo might be the most straightforward solution on the table.

The 35-year-old has starting experience, and he played under Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels while beginning his pro career with the franchise.

But Garoppolo's most recent start came in the final week of the 2024 regular season, when the Los Angeles Rams rested Matthew Stafford.

His last extended period as a starter was forgettable as well. Joining McDaniels on the Las Vegas Raiders in 2023, he had 1,205 passing yards, seven touchdowns and nine interceptions in six appearances.

The trouble for the Patriots is that the alternatives aren't much better. They could try to sign Will Levis from the New York Jets' practice squad, but he was a turnover magnet during his two years with the Tennessee Titans.

Nick Mullens is sitting on the Jacksonville Jaguars' practice squad, and the same goes for Jake Browning with the Los Angeles Chargers. Bailey Zappe is unsigned entirely.

Thanks to the Week 11 bye, coach Mike Vrabel and lead executive Eliot Wolf have time to deliberate over their next step. Whatever they decide, it's unlikely to give much reassurance to the fanbase.

articles.title: Cowboys defensive coordinator shows why he should be fired by asking Von Miller to cover Christian McCaffrey
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys asked Von Miller to cover Christian McCaffrey man-to-man on a cover zero blitz, and the 66-yard touchdown exposed a coaching flaw.
articles.body: By now everyone understands the Dallas Cowboys defense is, being professional here, horrible, terrible, awful, dreadful. And the one or two people left on Earth arguing otherwise can go look at one play that makes the case. The play came during the Cowboys' loss to the San Francisco 49ers in which the defense yielded 46 points and 584 yards and left pundits everywhere calling for the firing of Dallas defensive coordinator Christian Parker. COWBOYS' ELIJAH GARCIA GETS COMPLETELY FOOLED ON 49ERS' TRICK PLAY, UNDERSCORING POOR DEFENSIVE EFFORT IN LOSS The play is not the one in which Cowboys defenders ran the wrong way, chasing offensive players that didn't have the football. It's not the one where San Francisco's end around faked out all but one guy on the Dallas defense. Those are all physical problems. The players either couldn't get there or didn't want to get to the tackle. The play that speaks mostly to the Dallas problems, meanwhile, is evidence of a coaching problem. It was a 66-yard touchdown pass from Niners' quarterback Brock Purdy to running back Christian McCaffrey in which Parker asked Von Miller to cover the running back on the play. VON MILLER SIGNS WITH COWBOYS IN HOMECOMING MOVE FOR 2-TIME SUPER BOWL CHAMPION: 'LET'S MAKE THIS ONE SPECIAL' Miller, by the way, is an accomplished NFL pass rusher. He has 139.5 sacks in his career, which makes him a Hall of Fame candidate when he's done playing. But he's not a coverage linebacker. In fact, he's allowed 100 percent of the passes he's been asked to defend to be completed in three of the past four seasons. And did we mention, he's 37 years old? But the Cowboys somehow decided that asking their accomplished pass rusher not rush the passer and do what he's not good at, which is get in coverage, at age 37 years old, to cover one of the NFL's best pass-catching running backs, was a good idea. The play-call by Parker was a blitz. "Yes, it was cover zero," head coach Brian Schottenheimer admitted afterward. "All-out blitz." That means Miller had no help on the play. He had to cover man-to-man and the result was the 49ers scoring the points that ultimately decided this game. COWBOYS COACH BRIAN SCHOTTENHEIMER DEFENDS PLAYERS-ONLY MEETING DESPITE MIKE TOMLIN'S CRITICISM "Again, it's one of the situations [Parker] went with a call that he liked," Schottenheimer said, "and we got to look at it, but at the end of the day it didn't work out very well for us." Did Schottenheimer like the call? "I want to see the film," he said. That answer might be intended to protect his defensive coaches, particularly Parker. But too late, because the play laid bare how poorly thought-out their call was. It's not that a zero blitz is a bad call. It's that a zero blitz that doesn't consider the personnel on the field – in this case having Miller on the field to chase the much younger, much faster McCaffrey – is nonsensical. It glows in neon as a bad matchup. ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Any defensive coach who believes an opponent quarterback won't immediately go to his favorite receiver to take advantage of the matchup is simply not very good at playing chess because his move exposes his piece (Miller) to embarrassment. This, in short, is bad coaching. The Dallas Cowboys have a lot of issues with their defense. The Cowboys allow more yards per game than any other team and are third-worst in points allowed. And the snapshot of Von Miller chasing Christian McCaffrey on a 66-yard touchdown pass makes that point in living color. FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO
