articles.title: B/R Experts Week 11 NFL Power Rankings
articles.summary: We're 10 weeks into the 2026 NFL season—and playoff races are taking shape.
articles.body:
We're 10 weeks into the 2026 NFL season—and playoff races are taking shape.

After Minnesota's dominant win over the Packers at Lambeau Field and the Lions blowout victory in Germany, three teams in the NFC North are sitting at 7-2. The San Francisco 49ers are running away with the NFC West, but three teams in the division are 6-4 or better.

It's a similar situation in the AFC North, where Cincinnati's fifth straight win propelled the Bengals into first place. The NFC South is on pace to crown a "champion" with a sub-.500 record for the second straight year. And the NFC East has become the division no one wants to win after the first-place Giants stumbled against the Commanders.

As is the case most weeks in the NFL, Week 10 featured blowouts and nailbiters. Some games went according to script, while others threw it in the shredder. And the week's happenings shook up the NFL's pecking order from top to bottom.

As they do every week, Bleacher Report NFL analysts Gary Davenport , Kris Knox , Maurice Moton and Brent Sobleski have come together to sift through the week's action and how it affected that pecking order by ranking all 32 teams.

The bookends didn't change, but there was no shortage of shakeups between them.

ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN | CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND | JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN | NE | NYG | NO | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SEA | SF | TB | TEN | WAS

After back-to-back 11-win seasons, the Los Angeles Chargers entered 2026 with Super Bowl aspirations. Halfway through the month of November, the Bolts are still searching for their first win as they head to Baltimore to take on the Ravens Monday night.

It has been a truly disastrous season in Los Angeles, and Ian Rapoport of ESPN reported that major changes could be on the way once the nightmare ends.

"I would expect a pretty wholesale look at everything after the season," Rapoport said. "This is a place that really should win games. The acclimation process should be over. Everything that could go wrong has gone wrong."

One thing that apparently isn't changing is the quarterback. Per Rapoport, there is, "zero sense that they would move on from him at all."

Of course, one could argue there has been zero sense in L.A. all season long. – Davenport

Week 10 Result: Lost vs. Jacksonville 40-23

The Tennessee Titans continue to give their fans little to cheer about and just as little hope for the future. Trading standouts Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker at the deadline certainly didn't help matters.

Cam Ward continues to play like a below-average starter, which is never acceptable for a No. 1 overall pick. The defense underachieved even before parting with two of its best players, and it's fair to wonder if Robert Saleh could be one-and-done as Tennessee's coach.

The Titans haven't won at home since last December, and they won't be back in Tennessee until they host the Washington Commanders on December 6. -- Knox

Week 10 Result: Lost at Indianapolis 24-22

The Miami Dolphins are getting a good look at backup quarterback Kyle McCord while Malik Willis is on short-term injured reserve with a core muscle injury. He fell short trying to get the Dolphins into range for the game-winning field goal, but the second-year pro may be ready to serve as the team's primary backup.

McCord has at least three more weeks to audition for the entire league as Miami heads toward a third consecutive losing season. The Dolphins are a young team that's a quarterback and an offseason of free-agent additions away from playoff contention. -- Moton

The Indianapolis Colts got back in the win column on Sunday, though fans may not be thrilled about it. After trading away Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner, Josh Downs, and Keenan Allen, the Colts are clearly focused on the future.

That future probably won't include head coach Shan Steichen, and it may not include quarterback Daniel Jones, who posted a 41.5 passer rating in Sunday's win. The Colts fired GM Chris Ballard several weeks ago and could probably use a reset across the board.

Over the second half of the season, draft positioning should be more important to Indianapolis than wins over bad teams like Sunday's. -- Knox

The Arizona Cardinals pulled off a few big upsets in the first half of the regular season. However, now that injuries are beginning to take their toll, and the offense is reliant on rookie quarterback Carson Beck, the Cardinals may be done playing spoiler in 2026.

Beck appeared to be in over his head on his first career start, though a lot of quarterbacks are going to struggle against a defensive front led by Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett over the second half of the season. The more concerning issue is that Arizona is running out of healthy offensive playmakers, and its defense simply isn't very good.

The remainder of the Cardinals' season will be about seeing what they have in Beck and trying to maintain some confidence under first-year head coach Mike LaFleur. -- Knox

In terms of playoff aspirations, the New York Jets season is over by November—just like the last two seasons. If you could fast-forward time, Gang Green will likely be picking a new head coach from the offseason carousel.

Lead skipper Aaron Glenn has yet to lead the Jets to a division win (0-9). Over the last two weeks, the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills outscored Gang Green 66-24. Given the talent on the roster, the Jets have massively underachieved this season. -- Moton

The Philadelphia Eagles could look different heading into Week 11. The team has an opportunity to get healthier than it's been most of this season. Plus, a changed approach should be in the cards after losing seven straight games.

A bye week allows a coaching staff to reassess. In Philadelphia's case, a more simplified offense may be in the works.

"Yeah, we're looking at all that," head coach Nick Sirianni told reporters . "I think that especially with—I think that's definitely something we went through last week with that and we'll look more at that in the bye week."

If something doesn't change, things certainly will once the regular season comes to a close. Philadelphia is clearly in the middle of a soft reset, and someone else may be better suited to lead the team heads into the future. -- Sobleski

Head coach Kellen Moore should be embarrassed by his team's performance coming out of a bye week at home against a division opponent.

While some may view the New Orleans Saints' loss to the Carolina Panthers as a tight defensive battle that could've gone either way, it's inexcusable to go scoreless in the first half against a familiar opponent with extra time to prepare.

Under Moore, the Saints have routinely started slowly, ranking in the bottom five in first-half scoring for the last two seasons. This team needs a spark, and Moore probably isn't the coach who can provide it. -- Moton

Week 10 Result: Lost vs. Kansas City 35-13

You can't factor in rainy conditions or international travel in the Atlanta Falcons' last blowout loss. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes carved up the Falcons' lackluster defense, throwing for 348 yards and five touchdowns at Mercedes Benz-Stadium.

Atlanta's passing attack is broken, and star wide receiver Drake London is nicked up. Even in a winnable division, the Falcons are falling behind without solutions to issues on either side of the ball.

Also, it's no coincidence that Atlanta had its worst outing in pass coverage after trading safety Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars. We could see more quarterbacks having a field day against the Falcons in the second half of the season. -- Moton

If the Tampa Bay Buccaneers weren't in the NFL's worst division, they would be on the verge of falling out of playoff contention, but every team in the NFC South is under .500 entering Week 11.

After an 0-4 start, the Buccaneers went 3-2 and adopted a run-heavy offensive identity, racking up over 240 rushing yards in three of their last five games. While those numbers aren't sustainable, at least they have an offensive identity. That said, Tampa Bay didn't sign Baker Mayfield to a three-year, $165 million extension to lead a passing attack that has the fewest yards in the league.

According to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo , Mayfield suffered a lower leg injury in the Buccaneers' last outing against the Chicago Bears.

If the Buccaneers are going to make a run for the NFC South title, they need a healthy Mayfield. -- Moton

The Houston Texans' season isn't over just yet, but Sunday's loss to the Cleveland Browns was a major blow.

The Texans came out of their bye and delivered a convincing win in Week 9, albeit against the winless Chargers. Unfortunately, they were unable to build any momentum in Week 10. Instead, Houston blew an early 17-0 lead and slid further behind in the AFC South race.

C.J. Stroud has played well enough to finally earn his second contract, but little else has gone well for the Texans this season. The defense continues to underwhelm, and running back Woody Marks (concussion) joined David Montgomery on the injured list on Sunday. At this point, the playoffs are an extreme long shot. -- Knox

Week 10 Result: Won at New York Giants 24-21

Something important is happening with the Washington Commanders, because Jayden Daniels is starting to find his rhythm again.

Granted. Daniels threw two poor four-quarter interceptions. No one will deny those mistakes. However, the 2024 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year still led the game-winning drive directly after those poor decisions--which says a lot about where he's at in his development.

Furthermore, the quarterback is helping to elevate the play of those around him. Rookie wide receiver Antonio Williams and tight end Ben Sinnott were critical contributors during Washington's latest victory. The Commanders may still own a losing record and earlier concerns have not gone away entirely, but this team is starting to show signs of life, which portends good things for the future. -- Sobleski

Fernando-mania has officially arrived in Las Vegas. And for a moment, it appeared that Fernando Mendoza's first start was going to be a magical one—Mendoza led the Raiders to a touchdown on his first drive.

But the first NFL start for any quarterback is usually bumpy—even the first overall pick. And sure enough, for much of the rest of the game Mendoza looked like a first-year quarterback. He wasn't terrible, and the loss of tight end Brock Bowers to an ankle injury most assuredly didn't help matters. But Mendoza looked confused at times and held the ball too long, taking six sacks.

The reality is that when the Raiders traded Kirk Cousins, they essentially white-flagged the 2026 season. It's less about winning now than developing the team's franchise quarterback of the future.

In that respect, hanging around against the defending Super Bowl champions has to be at least somewhat encouraging. -- Davenport

Week 10 Result: Lost vs. San Francisco 46-40

The story remains the same for the Dallas Cowboys. The offense can consistently move the ball and score points, but the defense remains a constant source of disappointment.

The San Francisco 49ers offenses amassed a staggering 584 yards during Sunday's meeting. It's the most the team has accumulated during the Kyle Shanahan era, according to NBC Sports Bay Area's Matt Maiocco . The output was the most Dallas ever surrendered during a home game.

Once again, the Cowboys rank last in total defense. As The Ringer's Sheil Kapadia noted , the unit is also dead last in EPA per drive for the second straight season. Sadly, the Dallas offense is fun to watch but continues to be wasted, because the Cowboys somehow can't find a way to even slow an opponent. -- Sobleski

The Baltimore Ravens may be teetering on the brink of irrelevance, but the team isn't throwing in the towel.

Last week's trade for quarterback Jacoby Brissett isn't going to save the season. But it did show that the Ravens hope that Lamar Jackson will return at some point—the goal now is to shoot for 10 wins and hope it's enough.

Monday's visit from the winless Chargers will test that strategy soon enough. In a division where every other team is above .500, the Ravens can't afford a loss like that. -- Sobleski

Week 10 Result: Lost vs. Detroit 35-10 (Munich)

The New England Patriots left Munich, Germany, banged up. Drake Maye went down with an ankle injury on the first drive, and wideout A.J. Brown exited early with a hamstring issue.

The Patriots will have a Week 11 bye to recover, but Maye's status will determine how serious this team is as a contender when they return to action after Thanksgiving. Backup quarterback Tommy DeVito isn't leading this team to the playoffs. -- Moton

Week 10 Result: Won at New Orleans 20-17

The Carolina Panthers beat the New Orleans Saints, but they haven't snapped out of their offensive funk. Running back Chuba Hubbard is the focal point on that side of the ball, but until Bryce Young looks like the quarterback who started the season strong, the Panthers will have a low ceiling.

To get Young back on the right track for a string of games, the offensive line must do a better job protecting him. He's taken at least three sacks in four straight games. After snapping a three-game losing streak, Carolina has more room for improvement. -- Moton

Week 10 Result: Lost vs. Washington 24-21

Ultimately, the New York Giants fell late in the contest by allowing Stefon Diggs to split the defense for the game-winning score with under one minute left to play. Even so, an interesting situation continues to develop based on JJ McCarthy's play.

Jaxson Dart is the Giants' future at quarterback, right? To quote the great Lee Corso, "Not so fast, my friends."

McCarthy has legitimately shown growth potential during his short time at the helm of the Giants' offense. Thursday's loss doesn't take away from that possibility. Keep in mind, McCarthy and Dart are the same age. There's nothing saying the organization has to stick with one over the other. Instead, general manager Joe Schoen and head coach John Harbaugh can watch and see how this season unfolds, make a decision as to which they prefer and possibly use the other as a valuable trade chip. -- Sobleski

The resiliency now found within the Cleveland Browns roster is something to behold. After decades of a losing culture, where Cleveland found creative ways to fail on a near-weekly basis, the current lineup is filled with exciting young talent that simply doesn't know any better when it comes to the Browns' ineptitude over the past quarter-century.

Obviously, there's a reason why the saying "The Browns is the Browns" exists. Now, Cleveland is finding ways to win even when the odds are stacked against the team. For example, the Houston Texans led 17-0 at halftime. Once again, the Browns defense made life difficult on its opponent and provided an opportunity for the Deshaun Watson-led offense to chip away at the deficit before making big plays down the stretch.

The 1980 Browns were known as the Kardiac Kids. Forty-six years later, Cleveland is recapturing the magic that was once seen just off the shore of Lake Erie. -- Sobleski

Week 10 Result: Lost at Cincinnati 38-18

The Pittsburgh Steelers are limited. They may own a 6-3 record, with a legitimate chance to make the 2026 postseason, but Mike McCarthy's squad lacks the offensive firepower and defensive tenacity to be considered an actual contender.

Really, very little has changed this season despite the coaching change. The Steelers are basically the same team they were the last eight seasons under Mike Tomlin's supervision.

Sunday's matchup against the Bengals was particularly illuminating, because Pittsburgh's defense couldn't even slow Joe Burrow and Co. Furthermore, the Steelers didn't have an answer once Cincinnati shut down running back Jaylen Warren. -- Sobleski

Week 10 Result: Lost vs. Minnesota 30-10

After boatracing the Patriots in New England last week, the Packers entered Week 10 as hot as any team in the league.

They left it the team that got boatraced—at home.

The Packers were dominated in just about every facet of the game, Their high-octane passing game was stymied, with Jordan Love managing just 220 passing yards and one score while being dropped eight times. While speaking to reporters after the loss, head coach Matt Lafleur admitted his team got their butts kicked.

"This is a humbling league," LaFleur said. "And today we got humbled."

Green Bay now gets an off week to lick their wounds, but they also need to figure some things out—two of their next three are against the Rams and Bills, and now two back in the loss column in the NFC North the Packers are running thin on margin for error. -- Davenport

The Los Angeles Rams won their first game since placing Puka Nacua on injured reserve with a knee injury. They did so in a convincing fashion and showed that they have enough offensive talent to field a functional offense while Nacua and Davante Adams are sidelined.

However, there's a big difference between having a capable offense and being a top-tier Super Bowl threat. Los Angeles could still be the latter, and it is on a four-game winning streak, but it is about to face a higher degree of difficulty.

After their Week 11 bye, the Rams will face a brutal stretch that includes games against the Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs, San Francisco 49ers, Dallas Cowboys, and Seattle Seahawks (twice). -- Knox

The Seattle Seahawks continue to stay afloat with backup quarterback Drew Lock behind center. A 6-4 record may not be what Seattle envisioned, and it may be too late for the Seahawks to play catch-up in the NFC West. However, getting into the postseason should be the primary goal for the defending champs right now.

Seattle's defense is still championship-caliber, and its ground game is starting to come together with Zach Charbonnet and Jadrian Price both healthy. If the Seahawks can reach the playoffs and get reliable quarterback play in the postseason, they're fully capable of making another run.

The big unknown is when starting QB Sam Darnold (quad/rib) will return and whether he can shake the turnover issues that have plagued him in 2026. – Knox

Week 10 Result: Won vs. New England 35-10 (Munich)

When the Lions play like they did Sunday in Germany, they are more than capable of winning the Super Bowl.

The offense is as loaded as any in the league. Jared Goff topped 300 passing yards and threw three touchdown passes. Running back Jahmyr Gibbs had over 250 total yards and scored twice. So did wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown on a pair of long catch-and-runs.

It's a defense that is vastly improved over the last month that really puts the Lions over the top when everything is working, and that defense suffered a potentially catastrophic loss in Week 10. While celebrating a first quarter sack, star edge-rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffered a knee injury, and the fear is that injury is season-ending.

If that's the case, the Lions are in trouble in the NFC North—and done as a legit contender to rep the NFC in Super Bowl LXI. -- Davenport

Sunday in Atlanta, the Chiefs were without the services of the engine that has driven the offense this season—running back Keneth Walker III missed the game with a groin injury.

You wouldn't know it from the final score.

Patrick Mahomes accounted for all five Chiefs touchdowns—not bad for a guy with an ouchie elbow. Two touchdown passes went to rookie tailback Emmett Johnson, who tallied 171 total yards in Walker's stead. Wide receiver Josh Downs found the end zone in his first game with the Chiefs.

After the Chiefs dismissed the Falcons, head coach Andy Reid lauded the contributions the youngsters made in stepping up for Kansas City in Week 10.

"There were some guys that stepped in and really helped us out today," Reid said. "For these young guys, they're getting better. We're one of the youngest teams in the league, and they're getting better every week."

The Chiefs have been a bit up and down. But on the "up" weeks they can beat anyone. -- Davenport.

Week 10 Result: Won vs. Pittsburgh 38-18

The Cincinnati Bengals are finally back where they belong as a Super Bowl contender, because Joe Burrow is healthy, the team's offensive line is playing at a high level, wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins form a special duo and the defense is playing well. A few of those things haven't always been true, which is exactly why the Bengals haven't made a postseason appearance since the 2022 campaign.

Now, everything has fallen into place. As a result, Burrow has reached his final form. His command of Cincinnati's offense and ability to throw the ball anywhere he wants are special. The Bengals quarterback currently leads the NFL in completion percentage, passing yards, passing touchdowns, QBR and passer rating.

After Sunday's victory, Cincinnati sits all alone atop the AFC North. However, the Bengals should be viewed as a legitimate Super Bowl contender with how well the team is playing as a complete unit and not just relying on one or two superstars. -- Sobleski

Well, now we know what the Vikings look like with an offense.

The dominant storyline around Sunday's Lambeau Lambaste will undoubtedly be the return of quarterback Kirk Cousins to the Twin Cities, and rightly so—"Kirko Chainz" has been back less than a week and Minnesota looked as good offensively as it ever has in 2026. Star wideout Justin Jefferson told reporters that the game just had a different feel than in previous weeks.

"His composure, his confidence in the huddle, all of that, it definitely created a positive vibe," Jefferson said.

But as has been the case all year long, this is a team driven by a dominant defense that just smothered Green Bay's allegedly formidable passing game. The Vikings were all up in Jordan Love's business to the tune of eight sacks.

Add even a competent offense, and you have a legitimate Super Bowl contender. -- Davenport

The Denver Broncos have been a weird team this season.

As Denver's record indicates, the Broncos are winning a lot more than they are losing. But how they are winning is what's weird. Over the first three quarters of many games, Denver has looked average. Quarterback Bo Nix appears beatable. But then the fourth quarter starts, and the Broncos go full buzzsaw.

As Cecil Lammey of 104.3 The Fan in Denver said, Nix's play this year has been both impressive and concerning.

"Bo Nix has been pretty bad for most of this season," Lammey said. "Now if we based it on 4th quarter, his 4th quarter grade would be like an A, or an A+. But I can't ignore the first 3 quarters. There's more of them. We have more bad football from Bo Nix this year, than we have good football."

You can't argue with the results. But it's fair to question whether Nix can continue pulling a rabbit out of his hat every week once we get into January. – Davenport.

That the Bears are a two-loss team sitting in third place in in the NFC North says something about just how brutally tough that division is. But that's where the Bears are right now—both the Minnesota Vikings and Detroit Lions are above Chicago in the standings by virtue of a better record in the division.

However, it's worth pointing out that Chicago's two losses in the division carry asterisks—the Bears lost to the Vikings in a driving rainstorm and fell to the Packers with a backup quarterback under center.

The logjam atop the division sets up a fascinating stretch run—the Bears take on the Lions in Detroit on Thanksgiving, host the 6-4 Packers on Christmas and then close with Detroit at home and at Minnesota.

Those three straight divisional games to end the year are going to determine whether the Bears repeat as division champs. -- Davenport

The Jacksonville Jaguars might just be the most complete team in the AFC. They didn't look like that early in Sunday's game against the rival Titans, but they did eventually pull away to get their seventh win of the season.

Sunday's win was Jacksonville's fourth by three scores or more, and the Jags don't seem to have a glaring weakness on their roster. They should have a couple more strengths when they meet Tennessee again in two weeks.

Prized trade acquisitions Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis were held out of Sunday's game. -- Knox

The San Francisco 49ers continue to look like the best team in the NFC, though they did have some hiccups against the Cowboys on Sunday.

Brock Purdy had another MVP-caliber outing, as Christian McCaffrey, Deebo Samuel, and other 49ers playmakers repeatedly knifed through Dallas' suspect defense. The deadline trade for receiver Keenan Allen paid immediate dividends, and it's fun to think about how potent the offense could be once Allen is fully integrated into the game plan and Mike Evans is healthy again.

However, San Francisco's pass rush continues to underwhelm, and its defense struggled overall in Dallas. Next week's matchup with the Kirk Cousins-led Vikings will be a massive test. -- Knox

Week 10 Result: Won at New York Jets 31-12

I ranked the Buffalo Bills No. 1 in these rankings last week, and that didn't change after they went on the road and thumped the New York Jets. Buffalo has faced backup quarterbacks Joe Fagnano, Carson Wentz and Cade Klubnik over the previous three weeks and will face Kyle McCord in Week 11.

Expect the Bills to continue their dominance for their sixth straight win and remain atop the power rankings. With all of the New England Patriots' recent injuries, Buffalo could be the first team to claim a division title shortly after Thanksgiving. -- Moton

articles.title: 10 Eagles things I think I think coming out of the bye week
articles.summary: Thoughts about the Eagles as they didn’t play this week.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles didn't lose this week — because they didn't play.

The bye week is normally a time for players to regroup and get healthy. There are a lot of players the Eagles could use back, but this is a team that's 2-7 with their season a lost cause. They haven't won a game since September 20, a good two months once Philadelphia returns to action against the Pittsburgh Steelers on November 22.

This was a good week to get away from the Eagles, but there are still eight more games to be played in his dismal season. A lot happened during the bye week, with the Eagles and around the NFL (there never seems to be a shortage of storylines in this league).

As the Eagles bye week came and went, here were a few things I noticed watching the NFL this weekend — and other sports.

Every year this seems to be a thing, even when the Eagles have a Super Bowl contending team. Outside of 2022 and 2024, there isn't much to brag about when it comes to watching the football teams play in the NFC East.

The Washington Commanders win over the New York Giants on Thursday night was a rough watch, but playing on a short week didn't help either of those teams either. I also wasn't impressed with the Giants' win over the Eagles in Week 9, wondering how New York was ahead of the Dallas Cowboys in the division.

Then, the Cowboys gave up 584 yards and 9.4 yards per play to the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. This comes a week after surviving against the Indianapolis Colts — who might be as bad as the Eagles.

The NFC East has a combined record of 14-21-2 — a .405 win percentage. The four NFC East teams are 7-14 against opponents not in the division — a .333 win percentage.

Who wins the NFC East is anyone's guess (it won't be the Eagles), but that division champion has the look of a one-and-done team in the playoffs. Dallas should be the best team in this division, but can't get out of its own way.

I spent the bye week going to see the Philadelphia Sixers on Sunday afternoon, and it's incredible how the vibes changed with this team over the last five months.

Even though the Sixers finally beat the Boston Celtics in the playoffs last year, that team wasn't going to win the championship as they were constructed. Mike Gansey changed the direction of this franchise in a month, getting Jaylen Brown followed by LeBron James in the blockbuster moves of the offseason.

Xfinity Mobile Arena was buzzing towards that team on Sunday, with every LeBron pass and brown shot. Not to mention Tyrese Maxey is one of the best scorers in the league and V.J. Edgecombe is a blossoming star.

The building erupted when Maxey lobbed an alley-oop to James, and had me reminiscing of how much fun that 2000-2001 team was that won the Eastern Conference.

The Sixers are everything the Eagles aren't right now. They have a lot of stars that are performing at a high level and they're fun to watch. They also win games, as their 11-3 record is second in the Eastern Conference, and their best start since 2000-2001.

With the Eagles season a lost cause, the Flyers being the Flyers, and the Phillies getting older, the Sixers are the only hope in Philadelphia for a championship in the coming months. This city used to have that vibe for the Eagles…

3. Why I think Nick Sirianni won't be back

Watching a few NFL games this weekend (and keep in mind I covered the league for a decade), other teams just are more exciting to watch than the Eagles. The San Francisco 49ers have an aging roster of skill players and create explosive plays on the regular.

The Cincinnati Bengals and Detroit Lions are the same way, even though those teams have their flaws. The Los Angeles Rams don't have Davonte Adams and Puka Nacua and the offense don't seem to miss a beat.

Why can't the Eagles get anything going on offense? This lies deeper than the team being on the QB5 and WR3 and WR4 as the starters as recently as last game. This offense was a problem last year when the Eagles had their skill players healthy and had the most expensive offense in the NFL.

The Eagles are only 20th in cash spending on offense (currently), but this unit is last in yards per game (260.4), yards per play (4.3), and 30th in offensive points per game (16.4). They lead the league in three-and-out percentage (42.9%) and are last in 20+ yard play percentage (3.5%). The Eagles are also 25th in explosive play rate (9.3%).

Sirianni has an offensive background, yet the Eagles offense gets worse every year — no matter the play caller. On top of the seven-game losing streak and his inability to fix what's broken, the NFL may have evolved past Sirianni.

The Eagles may have to change things up to keep up with the current NFL. Other teams are playing offense at a way different level than the Eagles.

Brown had degenerative knee issues during his time with the Eagles, and his production was slowly decreasing over the last few years in Philadelphia. brown's best years were with the Eagles, but he still had some good years in him once he was traded to the New England Patriots right?

The first year in New England has been a disaster — for Brown and the Patriots. Brown has 11 catches for 128 yards and 0 TD in four games, having three drops and battling numerous injuries to his ankle, knee, and hamstring.

Brown is averaging career-lows in yards per catch (11.6), yards after catch per reception (3.4), receptions per route (10.6%), receptions per target (42.3%), yards per route run (1.23), yards per target (4.92), and drop rate (12.0%). The Patriots gave up a 2028 first-round pick for this.

Give credit to Eagles general manager Howie Roseman. He had no other suitors for Brown and had to wait until the June 1-deadline to even deal Brown due to his contract and all the dead money tied into it. Roseman still got a first-round pick for Brown, not worrying about the year of the pick — but the value of it.

Brown can still turn things around in 2027, but his best football was clearly with the Eagles. The Patriots paid for past production.

DeVonta Smith has been out since Week 6 with a hamstring injury. He's only played in four games this season, totaling 26 catches for 310 yards and 2 TD, averaging a career-high 77.5 yards per game.

The Eagles really haven't gotten to see Smith perform as the WR1 since he's been battling this hamstring injury all season, and Smith only caught passes from Jalen Hurts for three games. He only played one game with Tanner McKee before the injury cost him the last three games.

Hopefully the hamstring injury is past Smith and he's back following the bye. The same goes for Dontayvion Wicks and his injury, as the Eagles need both wide receivers to have a pulse on offense.

The offense is hurting Smith's production too. He's averaging career-lows in yards per catch (11.9), yards after catch per reception (1.8), yards per target (7.56), explosive play rate per target (17.1%). The good news? Smith has a career-high in yards per route run (2.26).

Hopefully Smith can made the most out of this year, or at least help out whoever plays quarterback.

6. No more Hollywood Brown or Fred Johnson

The Eagles released Hollywood Brown and Fred Johnson during the bye week, cutting ties with a wide receiver who couldn't see the field and a swing tackle who wasn't playing over rookie Markel Bell.

Philadelphia signed Brown to a $5 million deal, and he had five catches for 63 yards in four games — or $1 million per catch. Brown couldn't get on the field over Makai Lemon (even when he was struggling) or Darius Cooper, so there was no need to keep him around on a 2-7 team.

Johnson's release is interesting, as he's likely a more competent option at right tackle than Bell right now. The Eagles have to play Bell the rest of the year, but Bell also has no veteran to push him in practice. Johnson may have given Bell the opportunity to reset before he takes the field again.

The Eagles also only have three tackles on the roster — Jordan Mailata, Markel Bell, and Lane Johnson (and Lane Johnson is retired). So they really only have two tackles available.

Someone is getting signed or called up from the practice squad. John Ojukwu or Kiran Amegadjie are the candidates there, and both deserve an extended look anyway. A move has to be made at tackle this week if the Eagles are just riding with Bell at right tackle.

The 2026 Eagles just have the vibe of the 1998 Eagles, a team that just rotated quarterbacks throughout the year. The only difference is the 2026 Eagles had a franchise quarterback that was lost for the year, so they're scrambling to pick up the pieces.

Tanner McKee wasn't good enough in his three starts, so Joe Milton is getting an extended look. The Eagles will likely start Milton more than three games, but if Milton doesn't play well in December — the front office and coaching staff will have to try something else.

This is where Payton comes in, as the Eagles will want to see how their fifth-round developmental quarterback looks at some point in a lost year. Maybe Payton is good enough to be the QB2 on this team. That's what the Eagles are trying to find out with Milton right now.

Whether it's in December or January, it's likely Payton starts a game at quarterback. Whenever he's ready.

I really don't know if Hurts can play football again, since the Eagles aren't giving any updates on his condition. Howie Roseman won't even have a post-trade deadline press conference to avoid any questions asked about Hurts.

The hope is Hurts is back as the Eagles quarterback for 2027, but his future playing football is uncertain right now. That's the reality the Eagles are facing.

The Eagles are in position for a top-5 pick right now. Do they use that pick to get a quarterback? Package the Jacksonville Jaguars' first-round pick to move up and get a quarterback they like — and develop for the future?

There's so much at play right now. If Nick Sirianni isn't back, the new head coach may want a different quarterback. Hurts may not be able to play football again, or Hurts returns and the Eagles keep things status quo.

There's too much with Hurts' situation that needs to be unraveled. Wish the Eagles would give an update on how he's doing, but alas. Things are business as usual there, when it shouldn't be.

9. Eli Stowers should see more snaps — even if he hasn't earned them

Since the 2026 Eagles season is a lost cause, the team should be giving their rookies more snaps. Makai Lemon has gotten those opportunities due to injuries at wide receiver, and had some highs and lows over the last three weeks. Markel Bell has struggled at right tackle, but the Eagles released Fred Johnson and eliminated any veteran competition there.

The Eagles haven't done that at tight end. Grant Calcaterra and Johnny Mundt are still with the team, playing over second-round pick Eli Stowers for TE2 snaps. Stowers still struggled with his blocking and injuries held him back at the start of the year, but he's healthy now and needs live reps.

Is there really a reason to play Mundt and Calcaterra when the duo give the Eagles nothing in the passing game? Why not see if Stowers can handle himself against NFL defenders, and if he can improve each week?

Stowers hasn't really earned those snaps yet, but this season has shifted to developing players. That includes Stowers, who should be getting more snaps with Lemon and Bell the rest of the way.

The Eagles need to see if Stowers can play. This is the ideal opportunity, especially since Mundt and Calcaterra likely won't be on this team next year.

Since the Eagles traded Jordan Davis — and got a 2027 first-round pick and 2029 second-round pick in return — that freed up the front office to pay Ojomo at some point this year.

Once the Eagles signed Jalen Carter, re-signing Ojomo seemed like a pipe dream. Carter and Davis were both amongst the highest-paid players at their position, and there was no way the Eagles had the cap space at defensive tackle to pay three of them.

The Eagles don't need a nose tackle if Vic Fangio retires, as Ojomo would be a better fit for whatever defense they run. Ojomo will also get an opportunity for more snaps the rest of the way in 2026.

Ojomo's numbers aren't great this year, as he doesn't have a sack and his pressure rate is down from 11.6% to 9.6%. He still has 21 pressures and five quarterback hits, and should be more productive with more snaps.

The Eagles pass rush has been underwhelming across the board, but Ojomo should have a strong finish to the season. If not, the Eagles may be able to sign him cheaper than his going rate at the beginning of the year — especially if they can get an extension done early.

Bonus: Shoutout to the Pope John Paul II football team. I'm an assistant coach for PJP (Royersford, Pa.) and just completed my first season on the staff. We finished 9-3 and fell to Pottsgrove in the District 1-AAAA title game Friday night, ending an impressive season.

I had a lot of fun helping out this team this year and we had a great group of seniors. There's something so fulfilling in coaching, even though we didn't meet our goal (it's hard to win championships). 9-3 is a successful year (8-2 in regular season) and the players should have plenty to be proud of, even if the loss hurts right now.

Wish the seniors the best of luck going forward. Great group to work with, as was the rest of the team. Can't wait for year two.

articles.title: Former NFL Player Who Suffered Infamous Injury Sends Powerful Message to Aidan Hutchinson
articles.summary: Former NFL kicker Bill Gramatica, who suffered an infamous celebration injury, shares an emotional message with Lions star Aidan Hutchinson.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson is facing another heartbreaking setback after reportedly suffering a season-ending torn ACL during Sunday's 35-10 victory over the New England Patriots in Germany. But someone who knows exactly what it feels like to suffer an injury while celebrating has offered the 26-year-old some powerful words of encouragement.

Former NFL kicker Bill Gramatica , whose own career became associated with an infamous celebration injury in 2001, spoke with ESPN's Mike Garafolo about Hutchinson's situation. And while the circumstances brought back some painful memories, Gramatica is convinced that Hutchinson will overcome this latest obstacle.

"It's going to sting for a while, but it won't define him," Gramatica said. "He's such an incredible athlete and he's going to come back."

For a player who has already battled back from one devastating injury, those words carry plenty of weight.

Bill Gramatica Knows What Aidan Hutchinson Is Going Through

Back in 2001, Gramatica was kicking for the Arizona Cardinals when he celebrated a made field goal by jumping into the air. Unfortunately, he landed awkwardly and tore his ACL, creating one of the most memorable celebration-related injuries in NFL history.

When Hutchinson suffered a similar injury while celebrating his first-quarter sack of Drake Maye on Sunday, Gramatica immediately began receiving messages about the incident. As Jacob Richman of MLive reported Monday , the former kicker acknowledged that his name tends to resurface whenever something like this happens.

"For some reason, people tend to remember me every time something like that happens," Gramatica said. "This is the most high-profile one I think we've seen."

But rather than focusing on the unfortunate similarities, Gramatica offered encouragement to Hutchinson.

"He's already playing with a chip on his shoulder, it feels like," Gramatica said. "So this is just going to add to that."

Gramatica also made it clear that he doesn't believe players should stop celebrating because of freak injuries.

"It's a freak thing and I would never tell anybody not to celebrate," Gramatica said. "I think it's the emotion, and that's the natural part of the game. It's not scripted, it just comes from the heart."

Unfortunately, Hutchinson isn't the first Detroit Lions player to suffer a devastating knee injury while celebrating a sack. Back in 2014, linebacker Stephen Tulloch tore his ACL after jumping into the air following a sack of Green Bay Packers quarterback Aaron Rodgers.

The similarities are difficult to ignore, especially considering both players suffered their injuries without being contacted during the celebration itself. Tulloch eventually returned in 2015, starting all 16 games and recording 107 tackles, including a career-high nine tackles for loss.

Hutchinson, meanwhile, is facing another lengthy recovery after initial testing reportedly revealed a torn ACL . Doctors are also concerned about possible additional meniscus damage , although further testing will be needed to determine the full extent of the injury.

The latest setback comes after Hutchinson missed most of the 2024 season with a broken leg before bouncing back with 14.5 sacks in 2025. He had already recorded six sacks through nine games this season and was once again among Detroit's most important defensive players.

Gramatica Offers Perspective on Hutchinson's Future

Perhaps the most meaningful part of Gramatica's message wasn't about football at all. Having lived through the frustration and public attention surrounding his own injury, the former Cardinals kicker believes Hutchinson will eventually view this difficult moment much differently.

"Injuries like (Hutchinson's) and football is nothing compared to what these families go through," Gramatica said. "That's why I'm saying it seems big to him now, but in the grand scheme of his life, it's going to be very minor."

It's a perspective that could be valuable for Hutchinson as he begins another difficult road to recovery. The Lions will certainly miss his production on the field, but Gramatica's message is a reminder that one unfortunate moment doesn't have to determine a player's legacy.

Hutchinson has already proven he can return from a devastating injury and play at an elite level. Now, he'll have an opportunity to do it again.

And as Gramatica made clear, this injury doesn't have to define him.

articles.title: Meet Fernando Mendoza’s Parents, Elsa and Fernando Mendoza Sr.
articles.summary: Fernando Mendoza, who made his NFL debut on Nov. 15, shares a deep bond with his parents, Elsa and Fernando Mendoza Sr.
articles.body:
Fernando Mendoza is the eldest son of Elsa and Fernando Mendoza Sr.

The Las Vegas Raiders quarterback was raised alongside his younger brothers in Miami

After dedicating his Heisman Trophy win to his mom in December 2025, he made his NFL debut in November 2026

Fernando Mendoza 's parents, Elsa and Fernando Mendoza Sr., were there to cheer him on when he made his NFL debut.

On Nov. 15, the Las Vegas Raiders quarterback made his first start since joining the NFL, and both of his parents were spotted in a suite showing their support.

Fernando is the eldest child of Elsa and Fernando Sr. In addition to Fernando, the couple also raised sons Alberto — who plays football at Georgia Tech — and Max in Miami.

The family of five appears to have a close bond. Notably, Fernando and Alberto have worked together to raise money and awareness for multiple sclerosis, which has affected Elsa for nearly two decades.

Throughout his football journey, Fernando has credited both of his parents for his work ethic and thanked them for their encouragement over the years. When Fernando won the Heisman Trophy in December 2025, he emotionally thanked his parents and called his mom his "biggest supporter."

Here's everything to know about Fernando Mendoza's parents, Elsa and Fernando Mendoza Sr.

Both Elsa and Fernando were college athletes

Fernando inherited athletic genes from both of his parents, as they both played sports at their respective colleges.

Fernando Sr. rowed at Brown University, while Elsa played tennis at the University of Miami, per USA Today and the Miami Rowing Club .

Elsa later wrote an emotional letter to her son in The Players' Tribune in December 2025, in which she revealed that she initially had hopes Fernando would choose a career in tennis.

"My dream was for you to play tennis like I did," she penned and added that she'd run him through her college tennis drills when he was a child.

Fernando Sr. won a gold medal in the rowing 1987 Junior World Championships and went on to row crew at Brown, where he studied biology.

He later received his medical degree at the University of Florida College of Medicine before his residency at Jackson Memorial Hospital in Miami and a fellowship at Boston Medical Center.

Fernando Sr. currently works as a medical director at Nicklaus Children's Health System in Miami, per his bio and LinkedIn .

They are parents to three sons, including Alberto, who is also a football player

Elsa and Fernando Sr. both grew up in Miami, but they moved to Boston in their early 20s. While they lived in Boston, Elsa became pregnant with Fernando when she was 25 years old, as she wrote in The Players' Tribune.

They expanded their family two years later when they welcomed son Alberto. They are also parents to son Max.

Just like his older brother, Alberto is also a quarterback. Both Fernando and Alberto led their high school to state football championships during their respective days as starting quarterback.

"They definitely push each other," their high school coach, Dave Dunn, told Indiana Public Media in September 2025. "There's a deep love, but also a competitive fire that makes both better."

In 2023, Alberto committed to Indiana and redshirted the following year before he started playing alongside his older brother as the Hoosiers' backup quarterback in the 2025-2026 season. Alberto later credited Fernando for giving him the push to choose Indiana.

"I think having my little brother there, who's my best friend and the person who pushes me the hardest, it was great to have that," Fernando told the Indy Star in January 2025, per USA Today .

The brothers frequently participate in videos and interviews together, including an October 2025 video with JLab Audio where they joked about their family dynamics.

"I would say that I'm the peaceful zen one that always calms it down between all three of us brothers," Fernando said, before Alberto interrupted him and said that that was "false."

Alberto transferred to Georgia Tech in January 2026, where he now plays for the Yellowjackets.

Meanwhile, Max — who is six years younger than Alberto — has dreams of becoming a sports broadcaster, as he shared with Kelsey Nicole Nelson in December 2025.

Elsa was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis when the boys were young

When Fernando and Alberto were young children, their mom, Elsa, was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis.

"I was diagnosed about 18 years ago, but of course you never knew that," she wrote for The Players' Tribune in December 2025. "You and Alberto were so young, and I was doing fine ... and mostly I didn't want you to worry. It just felt like this impossible thing to place on you guys."

Elsa wrote that she didn't tell her children about her diagnosis until 2020 when things went "downhill," and she realized that she couldn't travel to all their games.

"No amount of years could have prepared me for how hard of a conversation it ended up being," she recalled. "'Your mom has this degenerative disease ... and while we don't know how it will progress, it's going to start to affect us in a few ways.' "

Elsa praised her son for making her diagnosis "so much easier" and acting in the "sweetest, strongest, most Fernando way possible — by making me feel the exact opposite of embarrassed."

"You've made me feel seen," she continued, while citing the ways he'd give her "full debriefs" of the college visits she couldn't attend and making her laugh while carrying her up the stairs.

"You've always kept that same spark in your eye," she added. "No matter what kind of state I've been in, or day I've been having — you've never once looked away. You've never once treated me like I'm embarrassing, or deficient, or anything other than someone you love and are standing by."

As Fernando and Alberto's football profiles have skyrocketed in recent years, they have used their platforms to advocate for MS awareness and launched several fundraisers.

They have a fundraising page through the National MS Society and have raised nearly $400,000 as of November 2026.

"My mom means the world to me—she's the most caring and positive person I know—and I'll keep doing everything I can to support her and others living with MS!" Fernando wrote in the description.

In addition to national efforts, Fernando and Alberto have also worked with several restaurants to create menu items for which the proceeds are donated to the National MS Society.

Fernando has described his mom as his "biggest supporter"

On Dec. 13, 2025, Fernando was awarded the prestigious Heisman Trophy and shed tears while dedicating the honor to his mom in his speech .

"Mami, this is your trophy as much as it is mine," he said. "You've always been my biggest fan. You're my light, you're my why, you're my biggest supporter. Your sacrifices, courage and love, those have been my first playbook and the playbook I'm going to carry by my side throughout my entire life."

Fernando continued saying, "You taught me that toughness doesn't need to be loud, it can be quiet and strong. It's choosing hope. It's believing in yourself when the world doesn't give you much reason to. Together, you and I are rewriting what people think is possible."

In addition to dedicating the award to his mother, Fernando also took time to thank his father for "grounding me" and "holding me accountable."

"Thank you for reminding me that talent means nothing without discipline and consistency," he told his dad. "While I'm playing a team game, I'm learning to grow into a man, and you personify commitment. You picked all of us up whenever we've needed it most."

Elsa, Fernando Sr. and Max attended several Indiana games while Fernando and Alberto were on the team — including the 2026 Rose Bowl where the Hoosiers defeated the University of Alabama.

"We're just really happy for them," Fernando Sr. told WTHR in a postgame interview. "If anybody's gonna do it, it's gonna be Fernando and Alberto. The amount of work and dedication they put in preparing for the games and their love, the passion for football and for each other and for their teammates, I think it shows."

Elsa called the entire experience a "fairytale" and said that she was "eternally grateful" for the "amazing decision" of having her sons attend Indiana.

Fernando's parents have continued to show their support for him as he joined the NFL and were there to witness his first game with the Raiders in November 2026.

articles.title: ‘All he did was dump on Jalen Hurts, now look at him’: Shannon Sharpe does not hold back on A.J. Brown
articles.summary: Sunday, the New England Patriots suffered a 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany, dropping their record to 5-5. The Pats struggled overseas aft...
articles.body:
Sunday, the New England Patriots suffered a 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany, dropping their record to 5-5. The Pats struggled overseas after losing starting quarterback Drake Maye in the first quarter and superstar wide receiver A.J. Brown in the fourth quarter. The remainder of the season looks grey for New England, but with a bye week ahead, it may be time to adjust.

With Maye expected to miss an extended period of time with a lower-leg and ankle injury and Brown awaiting evaluation for his hamstring, the Patriots' offense looks to be deteriorating. The former Philadelphia Eagle has had a disappointing start in Foxborough, missing six games in his first season with the organization, and one NFL legend believes the eight-year veteran "brought this on himself."

After the Patriots' loss, former NFL star and Nightcap co-host Shannon Sharpe reacted to Brown's recent injury and his future in New England.

"Nobody's feeling sorry for A.J. because he brought this on himself," Sharpe said . "He dumped on Jalen Hurts when he was there. He b*tched and moped and moaned and complained when he was there. They were winning football games and he wasn't happy with his role. Even though, Joe, he went to the Super Bowl and he was unhappy because he didn't catch 10 catches for 200 yards. And all he did was complain, complain, complain, and complain. Now he got his a** in a worse situation than when he was at Philly."

During his time with Philly, Brown constantly shared his discomfort with the organization on social media and in press conferences. Eagles QB Jalen Hurts took most of the blame during their time together, despite delivering a Super Bowl championship. But Sharpe addressed his disapproval of Brown's actions, as African American quarterbacks already have it hard in the NFL.

"So why would you do that to the brother quarterback?" Sharpe added. "I understand how hard it is for guys like Jalen Hurts and how, bro, we only a couple of decades before Blacks even really got a true opportunity to play that position. Because when you were a Black quarterback in college, they move your a** to running back, wide receiver, you play DB. So, it's just only a couple of decades, right, that they've been allowed. And all he did was dump on Jalen Hurts. And now look at it."

Brown has struggled to play through contact on his downfield targets, and as he gets older and prior injuries loom, creating separation has become increasingly harder. Dropped passes and short-stopping routes have also plagued his season, leaving critics to question whether the team should move on from him after the season.

articles.title: Aggies 7.5-point Underdogs on the Road Against Oklahoma
articles.summary: Texas A&M will be the underdogs as the Aggies face OU in Norman
articles.body:
After three straight losses, Texas A&M will look to get back in the win column as they head to Norman to face the Oklahoma Sooners for the first time in over a decade. The Aggie offense was unable to get anything going against Tennessee at home in a 22-7 loss . The Sooners are 7.5-point favorites at home against Texas A&M per FanDuel after defeating Ole Miss 24-17. The over / under is set at 39.5.

Oklahoma is 6-4 on the year and has relied heavily on a disruptive defense in the wins they've notched. The Sooners recently fired OC Ben Arbuckle, and former NFL Tight End Jason Witten is now the playcaller for OU. The Sooners lead the Aggies 19-12 in the all-time series after the two schools spent time together in the Big 12 Conference. The last meeting between the two on the gridiron came back in the 2013 Cotton Bowl, where Heisman-winning QB Johnny Manziel led the Aggies to a 41-13 victory over the Sooners.

It's no surprise to see Texas A&M as more than a touchdown dog given how the Aggies have performed down the stretch. Alabama remains the only SEC foe the Aggies have scored a touchdown against on the road. Unless the offense experiences an unprecedented revival, Texas A&M is in for a long day en route to the seventh loss of the season and an elimination from bowl eligibility.

articles.title: Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald achieves major feat in win over Raiders
articles.summary: The Seahawks are road warriors under Macdonald
articles.body:
Mike Macdonald added another milestone to his tenure as coach of the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday with the team's road win over the Las Vegas Raiders . The victory moved Macdonald into a tie with Jim Harbaugh, Matt LaFleur, Sean McVay and John Harbaugh for fifth place in road wins by an NFL head coach through his first three seasons.

The four coaches tied with Macdonald each made an immediate impact with their franchises. Jim Harbaugh turned the San Francisco 49ers into a conference contender and led the club to a Super Bowl appearance. LaFleur guided the Green Bay Packers to sustained regular-season success and multiple deep playoff runs. McVay brought the Los Angeles Rams to the Super Bowl in his first season and later led the franchise to a championship. John Harbaugh established the Baltimore Ravens as a perennial playoff contender and delivered a Super Bowl title.

Since taking over the Seahawks , Macdonald has helped Seattle develop into a consistent winner. His teams have produced strong results on the road, competed for postseason positioning and maintained momentum early in the current season.

The win over the Las Vegas Raiders added another benchmark to Macdonald's resume while reinforcing Seattle's ability to succeed away from home.

articles.title: Jets coach Aaron Glenn reveals he gave up defensive play-calling ahead of Week 10 loss to Bills
articles.summary: Aaron Glenn took over defensive play calling in the offseason.
articles.body:
New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn was hired by the team thanks to his excellence as a defensive coordinator. But after the team struggled on defense during Glenn's first year as head coach, he decided to take over defensive play-calling duties in 2026.

That change lasted just nine games. Glenn told reporters Monday he gave up defensive play-calling ahead of the team's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills in Week 10, per ESPN.

Glenn said the move was made to help the team win games. He added that while Jets defensive coordinator Brian Duker called plays Sunday, Glenn was "very involved" in the team's scheme.

"I've said this and I will continue to do this: Anything I can do as a head coach to help us win games, I'm willing to do it," Glenn said. "I'm not afraid to do that. So I gave him the lead, but I was very involved in what we ran."

The change appeared positive initially, as the Jets (2-8) gave up just 10 points in the first half Sunday. But Buffalo's offense got rolling the second half, allowing the team to pull away.

The Jets ultimately gave up 31 points in a loss to the Bills. Though, in Duker's defense, facing Josh Allen in your first game as a defensive play-caller is among the toughest asks in the NFL. The Bills rank first in the NFL with 31.9 points scored per game. In that sense, Duker's defense actually held the team under its season-long average … barely. The Jets still allowed 31 points, so the team shouldn't start popping the champagne just yet.

Glenn was noncommittal on whether Duker would continue to call defensive plays for the Jets, per ESPN. It was the first time ever in Duker's career that he was tasked with calling plays in a game. The 37-year-old has spent time as an assistant and position coach during his career, but this is his first season as an NFL defensive coordinator.

The decision puts Glenn in a tough spot with seven games left in the regular season. Since being hired, Glenn is just 5-22 with the Jets. The team has shown some improvement on both offense and defense in 2026, but not enough to drastically alter its outlook. Unless that improvement starts leading to wins down the stretch, Glenn could be out of a job at the end of the year.
